docs.title: Day 1 · Greetings & Introducing Yourself
docs.text: Day1Phase 1 · English · Day 1 of 80 Done

docs.title: Greetings & Introducing Yourself
docs.text: Today's goal: greet anyone politely, introduce yourself in 30 seconds, and ask the first questions that start a conversation.

docs.title: Greetings: which one to use
docs.text:
Situation Greeting Reply Morning (until 12 pm) Good morning! Good morning! How are you? Afternoon (12–5 pm) Good afternoon! Good afternoon! Evening (after 5 pm) Good evening! Good evening! Friendly, any time Hi! / Hello! / Hey! (friends only) Hi! How's it going? First meeting Nice to meet you. Nice to meet you too. Leaving Bye! / See you tomorrow! / Have a good day! You too! / Bye! Take care.

\"Good night\" is only for leaving

"Good night" means goodbye at night, or before sleep. When you arrive in the evening, say "Good evening".

docs.title: "How are you?" and good answers
docs.text:
Question Natural answers How are you? I'm good, thanks. And you? / Not bad, thank you. How about you? How's it going? Pretty good! / Going well, thanks. How was your weekend? It was great, thanks. I visited my parents. What's up? (casual) Not much! / Just working. You?

Always ask back: "And you?" or "How about you?" It keeps the conversation going.

docs.title: Introduce yourself: the 4-line formula
docs.text:
Name → Work / Study → Where from / live → One personal detail

"Hi, I'm Ashish. I'm a software developer at a product company. I'm from Lucknow, but I live in Bengaluru now. In my free time, I like cooking and watching cricket."

Part Sentence starters Name I'm … / My name is … / You can call me … Work I work as a … / I work at … / I'm a … / I'm studying … Place I'm from … / I grew up in … / I live in … / I've lived in … for 5 years Personal I like … / I enjoy … / In my free time, I … / I'm interested in …

docs.title: First questions to ask someone
docs.text:
• What's your name? / Sorry, what was your name again?
  • Where are you from?
  • What do you do? (= What is your job?)
  • How long have you been here / in this company?
  • Do you live nearby?
  • What do you like to do on weekends?

docs.title: Conversation 1: meeting a new colleague
docs.text: PriyaHi! I don't think we've met. I'm Priya. YouHi Priya, nice to meet you. I'm Ashish. I joined the backend team on Monday. PriyaOh, welcome! Nice to meet you too. Where were you before this? YouI was at a fintech company in Pune for six years. PriyaThat's great. Are you from Pune originally? YouNo, I'm from Lucknow. But I've lived in Pune and now Bengaluru. How about you? PriyaI'm from Kochi. I've been here for three years. I'm on the mobile team. YouNice! I'd love to learn how the mobile app works. Maybe we can have lunch sometime? PriyaSure, let's do that this week. YouGreat. See you around, Priya!

docs.title: Conversation 2: meeting a neighbour
docs.text: NeighbourHello! Are you the new family in 304? YouYes, hello! We moved in last Saturday. I'm Ashish. NeighbourWelcome! I'm Mr. Sharma, from 302. How are you finding the building? YouIt's very nice, thank you. Everyone seems friendly. How long have you lived here? NeighbourAlmost ten years now. If you need anything, just knock. YouThat's very kind of you. Thank you, Mr. Sharma. Have a good evening! NeighbourYou too!

docs.title: Practice
docs.text:
1. Choose the right greeting.

  1. It's 9 am. You meet your manager. → ______
  2. It's 7 pm. You arrive at a party. → ______
  3. It's 10 pm. You leave a friend's house. → ______
Answers
  1. Good morning! 2. Good evening! 3. Good night! (or "Bye, have a good night!")

2. Write your 4-line introduction using the formula above, then say it out loud 3 times. Time yourself: it should take about 20–30 seconds.

3. Make the question. Write a question for each answer.

  1. ______? → I'm from Jaipur.
  2. ______? → I'm a data analyst.
  3. ______? → I've been here for two years.
Answers

docs.title: Day 2 · Building Sentences
docs.text: Day2Phase 1 · English · Day 2 of 80 Done

docs.title: Building Sentences
docs.text: Today's goal: put words in the right order and make clear, correct sentences: positive, negative, and with am / is / are.

docs.title: The basic English sentence
docs.text:
English has a fixed order. Most Indian languages put the verb at the end; English puts it second.

Subject → Verb → Object → Place → Time Subject Verb Object Place Time I drink tea at the office every morning. Priya fixed the bug in the payment service yesterday. We will deploy the update to production on Friday. My son plays cricket in the park after school.

Hindi vs English order

Hindi: Main roz subah chai peeta hoon (I every morning tea drink). English: I drink tea every morning. Subject, then verb, then the rest.

docs.title: am / is / are (the verb "be")
docs.text:
Subject be Example I am I am a developer. → I'm a developer. He / She / It / one person is She is at home. → She's at home. You / We / They / many are They are late. → They're late.

Use "be" for: who/what (I'm an engineer), where (He's in the meeting), how (We're tired), age (She's 28), and descriptions (The app is slow).

Common mistake

❌ I am work in Infosys. → ✅ I work at Infosys. (Don't use "am" with another action verb in the simple present.)

docs.title: Negative sentences
docs.text:
Type Positive Negative be The server is up. The server isn't (is not) up. be (I) I am ready. I'm not ready. Action verb (I/you/we/they) I like coffee. I don't like coffee. Action verb (he/she/it) He works on weekends. He doesn't work on weekends. Past We finished the task. We didn't finish the task. can I can come. I can't come. Subject + don't / doesn't / didn't + base verb

After doesn't / didn't, the verb goes back to its base form: ❌ He doesn't works → ✅ He doesn't work.

docs.title: Make sentences longer (and clearer)
docs.text:
Add details in the order: what → where → when → why.

  1. I called the bank.
  2. I called the bank this morning.
  3. I called the bank this morning about my blocked card.
  4. I called the bank this morning about my blocked card, because I couldn't pay at the shop.

docs.title: Conversation: at the reception
docs.text: ReceptionistGood morning. How can I help you? YouGood morning. I'm here for an interview. My name is Ashish Gupta. ReceptionistWelcome. Who are you meeting? YouI'm meeting Ms. Rao from the engineering team. The interview is at 10:30. ReceptionistOkay. She's in a meeting right now. Can you wait for ten minutes? YouSure, no problem. Is there a washroom nearby? ReceptionistYes, it's down the corridor, on the left. YouThank you. I'll wait here.

docs.title: Practice
docs.text:
1. Put the words in order.

  1. coffee / every day / drinks / she → ______
  2. in Pune / my parents / live → ______
  3. the report / sent / yesterday / I / to my manager → ______
Answers
  1. She drinks coffee every day. 2. My parents live in Pune. 3. I sent the report to my manager yesterday.

2. Am, is or are?

  1. The meeting ___ at 3 pm. 2. We ___ ready. 3. I ___ in the office today. 4. The new laptops ___ fast.
Answers
  1. is 2. are 3. am 4. are

3. Make these negative.

  1. The app works offline. 2. I am free today. 3. They called me.
Answers
  1. The app doesn't work offline. 2. I'm not free today. 3. They didn't call me.

4. Fix the mistake.

  1. I am stay in Bengaluru. 2. He don't like meetings. 3. Yesterday I go to office.
Answers
  1. I stay (or live) in Bengaluru. 2. He doesn't like meetings. 3. Yesterday I went to the office.

docs.text:

  • Say 3 negative sentences about things you don't like ("I don't like…")
  • Make one long sentence with what, where, when, why

docs.title: Day 3 · Yes/No Questions
docs.text: Day3Phase 1 · English · Day 3 of 80 Done

docs.title: Yes/No Questions
docs.text: Today's goal: turn any sentence into a yes/no question, and answer naturally. These are the most common questions at counters, in shops, and at work.

docs.title: Rule 1: with am / is / are, swap the order
docs.text: Statement: You are ready. → Question: Are you ready? Statement Question The train is late. Is the train late? You are free today. Are you free today? This seat is taken. Is this seat taken? They were at the meeting. Were they at the meeting?

docs.title: Rule 2: with action verbs, add do / does / did
docs.text:
Do / Does / Did + subject + base verb … ? Statement Question Note You like spicy food. Do you like spicy food? I / you / we / they → do She works here. Does she work here? he / she / it → does, verb loses -s They delivered it. Did they deliver it? past → did, verb goes to base The bus goes to MG Road. Does the bus go to MG Road?

Most common mistake

❌ Does she works here? ❌ Did you went? → ✅ Does she work here? ✅ Did you go? The do/does/did already shows the tense, so the main verb stays in its base form.

docs.title: Rule 3: with can / will / should / have (helper verbs), swap the order
docs.text: Statement Question I can pay by UPI. Can I pay by UPI? The shop will open at 10. Will the shop open at 10? We should book early. Should we book early? You have finished. Have you finished? There is a pharmacy nearby. Is there a pharmacy nearby?

docs.title: Answering yes/no questions
docs.text:
Question Short answer (natural) Full answer (clear) Is the train on time? Yes, it is. / No, it isn't. No, it's 20 minutes late. Do you take cards? Yes, we do. / No, we don't. Yes, we take all cards and UPI. Did you get my email? Yes, I did. / No, I didn't. Not yet. Could you send it again? Can I sit here? Sure! / Of course. / Sorry, it's taken. Sorry, my friend is sitting here. Have you eaten? Yes, I have. / Not yet. Not yet. Shall we go together?

Don't answer with only \"Yes\" or \"No\"

A bare "No." can sound rude. Add a little: "No, sorry, we don't." or "Yes, of course!"

docs.title: Polite yes/no questions you'll use every day
docs.text:
• Is this the queue for tickets?
  • Do you have this in a larger size?
  • Does this bus go to the railway station?
  • Can I pay by card?
  • Is there a lift / washroom / ATM nearby?
  • Did you get a chance to look at my PR?
  • Have you booked the tickets?
  • Are you using this chair?

docs.title: Conversation: at a medical shop
docs.text: YouHi. Do you have something for a cold? PharmacistYes, we do. Do you have a fever too? YouNo, I don't. Just a runny nose and a sore throat. PharmacistOkay. Is it for you or for a child? YouIt's for me. Can I take it with my blood-pressure tablets? PharmacistYes, that's fine. Do you have any allergies? YouNo, I don't. Is it okay to take it before food? PharmacistBetter after food. Take it twice a day. YouThank you. Can I pay by UPI? PharmacistSure. Scan the QR code here.

docs.title: Practice
docs.text:
1. Make yes/no questions.

  1. The shop is open. 2. You live near here. 3. He finished the work. 4. We can park here. 5. There is a lift.
Answers
  1. Is the shop open? 2. Do you live near here? 3. Did he finish the work? 4. Can we park here? 5. Is there a lift?

2. Fix the questions.

  1. You are coming? 2. Does he likes tea? 3. Did you saw the email? 4. Is available the room?
Answers
  1. Are you coming? 2. Does he like tea? 3. Did you see the email? 4. Is the room available?

3. Give a short answer and a full answer. "Do you work on weekends?" / "Is the office far from here?"

Sample answers

No, I don't. I only work Monday to Friday. / No, it isn't. It's about ten minutes by auto.

docs.title: Day 4 · Wh- Questions
docs.text: Day4Phase 1 · English · Day 4 of 80 Done

docs.title: Wh- Questions
docs.text: Today's goal: ask for any information you need (where, when, how much, how long, why) with the right word order.

docs.title: The question words
docs.text: Word Asks about Example What thing, information What is your name? / What time is it? Where place Where is platform 5? When time When does the shop open? Why reason Why is the flight delayed? Who person Who is the project manager? Which choice from a group Which bus goes to the airport? Whose owner Whose laptop is this? How way, method, condition How do I get to the metro? / How are you? How much price, uncountable amount How much is this? / How much water do you need? How many countable number How many people are coming? How long duration How long does the journey take? How often frequency How often does the bus come? How far distance How far is the hospital? What time exact time What time does the train leave?

docs.title: The formula
docs.text: Wh- word + helper (is/are/do/does/did/can/will) + subject + verb … ? Wh- Helper Subject Verb / rest Where is the ticket counter ? When does the train leave? How much did you pay? Why are you late? Which platform does the Chennai train leave from? How long will it take? What can I do?

docs.title: From statement to question: step by step
docs.text:
Statement: The bus leaves at 6.

  1. Find what you want to ask about: at 6 → a time → When / What time
  2. Add the helper: the verb is "leaves" (present, he/she/it) → does
  3. Base verb: leaves → leave
  4. Question: What time does the bus leave?
Statement Ask about Question She lives in Pune. place Where does she live? The room costs ₹3,000. price How much does the room cost? I'm late because of traffic. reason Why are you late? Ravi fixed the bug. person (subject) Who fixed the bug? They met last week. time When did they meet?

Special case: who / what as the subject

When who or what is the subject, don't add do/does/did: ✅ Who called you? (someone called) · ✅ What happened? · ❌ Who did call you?

docs.title: Indirect questions: more polite
docs.text:
Start with a polite phrase, then use statement order (no do/does/did):

Direct Polite (indirect) Where is the station? Could you tell me where the station is? What time does it open? Do you know what time it opens? How much does it cost? Can I ask how much it costs? When will it be ready? Could you let me know when it will be ready?

Use indirect questions with strangers, officials and senior people.

docs.title: Conversation: at a railway enquiry counter
docs.text: YouExcuse me. Which train goes to Mysuru this evening? ClerkThere's the Chamundi Express at 6:15. YouWhich platform does it leave from? ClerkPlatform 8. YouHow long does the journey take? ClerkAbout three hours. YouHow much is a second-class ticket? Clerk₹110. YouAnd how often do trains go to Mysuru on Sundays? ClerkEvery two hours, roughly. YouCould you tell me where the ticket counter for reserved tickets is? ClerkIt's on the first floor, near the escalator. YouThank you very much!

docs.title: Practice
docs.text:
1. Choose the question word: what, where, when, why, who, which, how much, how long.

  1. ______ is your office? (place) 2. ______ is this shirt? (price) 3. ______ did you call me? (reason)
  2. ______ colour do you want: red or blue? 5. ______ does the movie last?
Answers
  1. Where 2. How much 3. Why 4. Which 5. How long

2. Make a question about the bold part.

  1. The meeting starts at 4. 2. He bought a new phone. 3. We stayed for three days. 4. Meena booked the hotel.
Answers
  1. What time does the meeting start? 2. What did he buy? 3. How long did you stay? 4. Who booked the hotel?

3. Make these polite. "Where is the washroom?" / "When will my order arrive?"

Answers

Could you tell me where the washroom is? / Could you let me know when my order will arrive?

docs.title: Answering Questions
docs.text: Today's goal: answer questions clearly and politely: short or full, saying "no" politely, giving reasons, and saying "I'm not sure" without sounding weak.

docs.title: The answer ladder: choose your length
docs.text: 1. Short — "Yes, it is." · fast, casual, enough for simple facts 2. Short + detail — "Yes, it's on the second floor." · the most useful everyday answer 3. Answer + reason — "No, I can't come, because I have a client call." · for requests and decisions 4. Answer + reason + next step — "…but I can join at 5. Does that work?" · the most professional answer

docs.title: Answer the question that was asked
docs.text:
Question ❌ Unclear answer ✅ Clear answer When will it be ready? "We are working on it." "By Thursday evening." How much is the room? "It's a very good room, sir…" "₹3,500 a night, including breakfast." Where do you live? "Near." "In Indiranagar, near the metro station." Did you finish the report? "Actually I was doing many things…" "Not yet. I'll send it by 4 pm."

Answer first, explain after.

docs.title: Saying no politely
docs.text: Situation Polite "no" Offer No, thank you. / I'm fine, thanks. Request you can't do I'm sorry, I can't today. Could we do it tomorrow? Invitation Thank you so much for inviting me. Unfortunately, I have plans that day. Something not available Sorry, we don't have that. We have this instead. Disagreeing I'm not sure I agree. Here's why…

docs.title: When you don't know or aren't sure
docs.text: Instead of Say "I don't know." (and stop) "I'm not sure, but I'll find out and let you know." A guess presented as fact "I think it's on Friday, but let me confirm." Silence "Good question. Let me think for a second." Pretending you understood "Sorry, could you say that again?"

docs.title: Answers with numbers, places and time
docs.text:
• Time: "At half past six." / "Around 7." / "In about twenty minutes." / "By Friday."
  • Place: "On the second floor." / "Next to the bank." / "Opposite the bus stand."
  • Frequency: "Every day." / "Twice a week." / "Once a month." / "Hardly ever."
  • Duration: "For three years." / "Since 2021." / "About two hours."

docs.title: Conversation: the HR call
docs.text: HRHi, is this Ashish? I'm calling from Brightsoft about the backend role. YouYes, this is Ashish. Thanks for calling. HRIs now a good time to talk for ten minutes? YouYes, that's fine. HRGreat. How many years of experience do you have with Java? YouAbout nine years. I've used Java with Spring Boot for most of that time. HRAnd what's your current notice period? YouIt's sixty days, but it may be negotiable. HRAre you open to working from the office three days a week? YouYes, I am. The office is about forty minutes from my home. HRWhat's your expected salary? YouI'm not sure yet. I'd like to know more about the role first. Could you share the budgeted range? HRSure, I'll email it to you today. YouThank you. I'll look out for it.

docs.title: Practice
docs.text:
1. Give a short + detail answer.

  1. Is there an ATM near here? 2. Do you work from home? 3. Have you been to Goa?
Sample answers
  1. Yes, there's one next to the pharmacy. 2. Sometimes. I work from home on Mondays and Fridays.
  2. Yes, I have. I went there last December.

2. Say no politely.

  1. "Would you like some sweets?" (you're full) 2. "Can you work this Sunday?" (you can't)
Sample answers
  1. No, thank you. They look delicious, but I'm full. 2. I'm sorry, I can't this Sunday. I could work an extra hour on Monday and Tuesday instead. Would that help?

3. Rewrite the weak answer. "When will the fix be deployed?" → "Actually we are trying, maybe soon."

Sample answer

"Today by 6 pm. We're running the final tests now."

docs.text:

  • Say no politely once, with a reason and an alternative
  • Use "I'm not sure, but I'll find out" instead of guessing

docs.title: Day 6 · Present: Routines & Right Now
docs.text: Day6Phase 1 · English · Day 6 of 80 Done

docs.title: Present: Routines & Right Now
docs.text: Today's goal: talk about your daily routine (present simple) and what's happening now (present continuous), and ask questions with both.

docs.title: Two presents, two jobs
docs.text: Present simple Present continuous Use for habits, routines, facts right now, these days, temporary Form I work · She works I am working · She is working Key words always, usually, every day, on Mondays now, right now, at the moment, today, this week Example I take the metro to work. I'm taking an auto today because the metro is closed.

docs.title: Present simple
docs.text:
I / you / we / they + verb · he / she / it + verb + s Positive Negative Question I start work at 9. I don't start work at 9. Do you start work at 9? She lives in Chennai. She doesn't live in Chennai. Does she live in Chennai? The shop closes at 10. The shop doesn't close at 10. When does the shop close?

Spelling: work → works · watch → watches · go → goes · study → studies · have → has

How often: always (100%) → usually → often → sometimes → rarely → never (0%). Position: before the main verb (I usually walk), after be (I'm always late).

docs.title: Present continuous
docs.text:
am / is / are + verb-ing Positive Negative Question I'm working from home today. I'm not working today. Are you working today? He's talking to the client. He isn't talking to the client. Who is he talking to? They're building a new app. They aren't building it. What are they building?

Some verbs are not used in -ing (state verbs)

know, understand, want, like, need, believe, own, belong, seem. ❌ I am knowing him. ❌ I am having two kids. ✅ I know him. ✅ I have two kids.

docs.title: Your daily routine: useful sentences
docs.text:
• I wake up at 6:30 and go for a walk.
  • I have breakfast at 8 and leave for work at 8:45.
  • I usually take the metro; it takes about 35 minutes.
  • We have a stand-up meeting at 10.
  • I get back home around 7 and spend time with my kids.
  • On weekends, I play badminton and visit my parents.

docs.title: Conversation: catching up with a friend
docs.text: FriendHey! What are you doing these days? YouI'm working on a new project at work. We're building a delivery app. FriendNice! Do you still work from home? YouNot every day. I go to the office three days a week now. FriendHow do you get there? YouI usually take the metro. But this week I'm driving, because the metro line is closed for repairs. FriendAnd are you still playing badminton? YouYes, I play every Saturday morning. Do you want to join us? FriendSure! What time do you start? YouWe start at seven. I'll send you the location.

docs.title: Practice
docs.text:
1. Simple or continuous?

  1. She ______ (work) at a bank. 2. Look! It ______ (rain). 3. I ______ (not like) long meetings.
  2. We ______ (have) lunch now. Can I call you back? 5. The train usually ______ (leave) on time.
Answers
  1. works 2. is raining 3. don't like 4. are having 5. leaves

2. Make questions.

  1. (you / usually / get up / when) 2. (he / work / today / from home) 3. (what / you / do / now)
Answers
  1. When do you usually get up? 2. Is he working from home today? 3. What are you doing now?

3. Fix the mistakes. He go to gym daily. / I am understanding. / She is work in Wipro.

Answers

He goes to the gym every day. / I understand. / She works at Wipro.

docs.text:

docs.title: Day 7 · Past: What Happened
docs.text: Day7Phase 1 · English · Day 7 of 80 Done

docs.title: Past: What Happened
docs.text: Today's goal: talk about yesterday, last week and your experience: what happened, what went wrong, and what you did about it.

docs.title: Past simple: finished actions
docs.text: Regular: verb + -ed · Irregular: learn the form · Questions & negatives: did + base verb Positive Negative Question I called the bank. I didn't call the bank. Did you call the bank? She went to Delhi. She didn't go to Delhi. Where did she go? The app crashed. The app didn't crash. Why did the app crash? It was late. / They were late. It wasn't late. Was it late?

docs.title: 30 irregular verbs you use every day
docs.text: Base Past Base Past Base Past be was / were get got pay paid buy bought give gave put put bring brought go went read read come came have had say said do did hear heard see saw drink drank keep kept send sent drive drove know knew sit sat eat ate leave left speak spoke feel felt lose lost take took find found make made tell told

docs.title: Telling a story in order
docs.text:
Use sequence words: First… · Then… · After that… · Suddenly… · Finally…

"Yesterday I left home at 8. First, I took an auto to the station. Then I found that my train was two hours late. So I called my manager and told her. Finally, I worked from the station café and joined the 11 o'clock meeting on my phone."

docs.title: Present perfect: experience and recent results
docs.text:
have / has + past participle (been, done, seen, gone, eaten…) Use Example Life experience (no time given) Have you ever been to Kerala? · I've never flown business class. Recent result that matters now I've lost my wallet. (I don't have it now) · The flight has landed. Up to now (with for / since) I've worked here for five years / since 2021.

Past simple vs present perfect

With a finished time (yesterday, last year, in 2020), use past simple: ❌ I have seen him yesterday. → ✅ I saw him yesterday.

docs.title: Conversation: reporting a problem at the hotel desk
docs.text: YouGood morning. I had a problem in my room last night. ReceptionistI'm sorry to hear that. What happened? YouThe AC stopped working at around midnight. I called the front desk, but nobody answered. ReceptionistI apologise. Did anyone come to check it? YouNo, nobody came. I didn't sleep well because it was very hot. ReceptionistI'm really sorry. Have you checked out yet? YouNot yet. I'm leaving at 11. ReceptionistI've informed the manager. We'll give you a 20% discount on last night's stay. YouThank you, I appreciate that.

docs.title: Practice
docs.text:
1. Past form. go, buy, send, pay, meet, write, forget, think

Answers

went, bought, sent, paid, met, wrote, forgot, thought

2. Make questions about yesterday.

  1. (you / go / where) 2. (she / pay / how much) 3. (the meeting / start / what time)
Answers
  1. Where did you go? 2. How much did she pay? 3. What time did the meeting start?

3. Past simple or present perfect?

  1. I ______ (live) in Hyderabad in 2019. 2. ______ you ever ______ (try) Kerala food?
  2. Oh no, I ______ (forget) my ID card! 4. We ______ (meet) last Friday.
Answers
  1. lived 2. Have … tried 3. have forgotten / I've forgotten 4. met

docs.title: Day 8 · Future: Plans & Promises
docs.text: Day8Phase 1 · English · Day 8 of 80 Done

docs.title: Future: Plans & Promises
docs.text: Today's goal: talk about plans, predictions, promises and arrangements, and ask people about theirs.

docs.title: Three ways to talk about the future
docs.text: Form Use for Example will + verb decisions now, promises, offers, predictions I'll call you back. · It will rain later. going to + verb plans you already decided; clear evidence I'm going to buy a new laptop. · Look at those clouds, it's going to rain. present continuous fixed arrangements (time/place agreed) I'm meeting the client at 3 tomorrow. · We're flying to Delhi on Friday.

docs.title: will
docs.text:
Positive Negative Question I'll send it today. I won't (will not) be late. Will you be there? It'll be ready by 5. It won't take long. When will it be ready?

Promises & offers: "I'll fix it tonight." · "I'll help you with that." · "Shall I book a cab?" (Shall I / we = offer or suggestion.)

docs.title: going to
docs.text: Positive Negative Question We're going to move to Pune. I'm not going to take the job. Are you going to apply?

docs.title: Talking about plans & time
docs.text:
• this evening / weekend · next week / month / year · in two days / an hour
  • tomorrow morning · the day after tomorrow · by Friday (= not later than Friday)
  • until 6 (= continuing up to 6) · soon · later today

docs.title: Questions about plans
docs.text:
• What are you doing this weekend?
  • Are you going to take any leave this year?
  • When will you know the result?
  • Will you be free after lunch?
  • What time are you leaving tomorrow?

docs.title: Conversation: planning a weekend trip
docs.text: FriendAre you doing anything this weekend? YouYes! We're going to Coorg on Saturday morning. FriendNice! How are you getting there? YouWe're driving. We're going to leave at six to avoid traffic. FriendWhere are you staying? YouWe've booked a homestay near Madikeri. We're coming back on Sunday evening. FriendSounds lovely. Will it be cold? YouProbably. I'll pack some jackets. FriendSend me photos! YouI will. I'll message you when we get there.

docs.title: Practice
docs.text:
1. will, going to, or present continuous?

  1. A: "The phone is ringing." B: "I ______ (answer) it."
  2. We ______ (visit) my parents next Sunday. It's all planned.
  3. I promise I ______ (not tell) anyone.
  4. I've decided: I ______ (learn) Kubernetes this year.
Answers
  1. 'll answer 2. are visiting (or are going to visit) 3. won't tell 4. 'm going to learn

2. Make questions. (you / do / tonight / what) · (the results / be / ready / when) · (you / apply / for the job)

Answers

What are you doing tonight? · When will the results be ready? · Are you going to apply for the job?

3. Write 3 plans for next week: one with going to, one arrangement with time, one promise with will.

docs.title: Day 9 · Polite Requests & Offers
docs.text: Day9Phase 1 · English · Day 9 of 80 Done

docs.title: Polite Requests & Offers
docs.text: Today's goal: ask for things, offer help, ask permission and refuse, politely. The same words sound rude or kind depending on how you build the sentence.

docs.title: The politeness ladder
docs.text: Give me the bill. — an order; sounds rude Can I have the bill? — fine with friends, shops, cafés Could I have the bill, please? — polite: use this as your default Would you mind bringing the bill? — very polite I was wondering if you could… — very formal; for big requests and senior people

docs.title: Requests: asking someone to do something
docs.text:
Pattern Example Can you + verb…? Can you send me the link? Could you + verb…, please? Could you speak a bit slower, please? Would you + verb…? Would you check this for me? Would you mind + verb-ing…? Would you mind closing the window? Do you think you could…? Do you think you could review my PR today?

Answering "Would you mind…?": "No, not at all." = Yes, I'll do it! (because "mind" = object).

docs.title: Asking for things
docs.text:
• Could I have a glass of water, please?
  • I'd like (= I would like) a window seat, please.
  • Can I get a medium cappuccino? (cafés)
  • Do you have this in black?

docs.title: Asking permission
docs.text: Pattern Example Reply Can I…? Can I sit here? Sure. / Go ahead. Could I…? Could I leave 30 minutes early today? Yes, that's fine. May I…? (formal) May I come in? Please do. Is it okay if I…? Is it okay if I join by phone? Of course. Do you mind if I…? Do you mind if I open the window? No, go ahead.

docs.title: Offers and suggestions
docs.text:
• Shall I call a cab for you?
  • Would you like some tea? → Yes, please. / No, thank you.
  • Can I help you with that bag?
  • Let me help you. / Let me check that for you.
  • Why don't we take a break? / How about meeting on Monday? / Let's order lunch.

docs.title: Refusing politely
docs.text:
• "I'm sorry, I'm afraid I can't today."
  • "Thanks for asking, but I have another commitment."
  • "I'd love to, but I'm travelling that week."
  • "Unfortunately, that's not possible. What I can do is…"

docs.title: Magic words & phrases
docs.text: Instead of Say "What?" "Sorry? / Pardon? / Sorry, could you repeat that?" "Wait." "Just a moment, please. / Could you give me a minute?" "I want…" "I'd like…" "Give…" "Could you pass… / Could I have…" "Move." "Excuse me, could I get past?" "Tell me." "Could you let me know…?" "No problem" (after thanks) "You're welcome. / My pleasure. / Happy to help."

docs.title: Conversation: asking a colleague for help
docs.text: YouHi Meena, do you have a minute? MeenaSure, what's up? YouI was wondering if you could help me with the Kafka configuration. I'm a bit stuck. MeenaOf course. Would you mind waiting until 3? I'm in a meeting till then. YouNot at all. Shall I send you the error log before that? MeenaYes, please. That would help. YouGreat, I'll send it now. And is it okay if I share my screen when we talk? MeenaAbsolutely. YouThanks so much, I really appreciate it. MeenaHappy to help!

docs.title: Practice
docs.text:
1. Make these polite.

  1. Give me the menu. 2. Repeat that. 3. I want to change my seat. 4. Wait here.
Answers
  1. Could I have the menu, please? 2. Sorry, could you repeat that, please? 3. I'd like to change my seat, if possible. 4. Could you wait here for a moment, please?

2. Reply. "Would you mind turning off your phone?" (You agree.) / "Would you like some coffee?" (You don't want it.)

Answers

No, not at all. (and turn it off) / No, thank you. I'm fine.

3. Refuse politely. Your colleague asks you to stay late tonight to test their feature.

Sample answer

I'd love to help, but I can't stay late tonight. I could test it first thing tomorrow morning. Would that work?

docs.title: Speak today
docs.text:
• Use Could I…? or Could you…? at least 5 times
  • Replace one "What?" with "Sorry, could you repeat that?"
  • Offer help once with "Shall I…?" or "Let me…"

docs.title: Day 10 · Joining Ideas & Opinions
docs.text: Day10Phase 1 · English · Day 10 of 80 Done

docs.title: Joining Ideas & Opinions
docs.text: Today's goal: join short sentences into longer, natural ones, give reasons, and share, agree with or disagree with an opinion.

docs.title: Linking words
docs.text:
Word Job Example and add I booked the tickets and paid online. but contrast The hotel was nice, but the food was average. because reason I was late because the metro stopped. so result The metro stopped, so I was late. or choice We can take a cab or walk. if condition If it rains, we'll stay home. when time When I reach the station, I'll call you. although / even though surprising contrast Although it was expensive, it was worth it. also / too add I also need a receipt. / I need a receipt too. however contrast (formal, new sentence) The plan is good. However, it's risky. for example example We need better tests, for example for the payment flow.

Don't double up

❌ Although it was late, but I went. → ✅ Although it was late, I went. or ✅ It was late, but I went. ❌ Because I was sick, so I didn't come. → ✅ Because I was sick, I didn't come.

docs.title: if sentences (conditions)
docs.text: Type Pattern Example Real / likely If + present, will + verb If the train is late, I'll take a cab. Always true If + present, present If you press this, the light turns on. Imaginary If + past, would + verb If I had more time, I would learn French.

docs.title: Giving opinions
docs.text:
Opinion Agree Disagree (politely) I think… I agree. / Exactly! / That's true. I'm not sure about that. In my opinion… I feel the same way. I see it a bit differently. I feel that… You're right. That's a good point, but… If you ask me… Absolutely. I agree up to a point, but… I'd say… Good point. I'm afraid I don't agree, because…

Give a reason: "I think we should take the train, because it's faster than the bus and we can work on the way."

docs.title: Conversation: deciding where to eat
docs.text: ColleagueWhere should we go for the team lunch? YouI think we should try the new Andhra place, because everyone likes spicy food. ColleagueThat's true, but it's a bit far. It takes twenty minutes to get there. YouGood point. If we leave at 12:30, we'll be back by 2. Although it's far, the food is really good. ColleagueHmm. What about the vegetarians? YouThey have a big vegetarian menu too, so it should be fine. ColleagueOkay, I agree. Let's book a table for ten. YouGreat. I'll call them now and book it.

docs.title: Practice
docs.text:
1. Join with and, but, because, so.

  1. It was raining. I took an umbrella. 2. I like my job. It's very stressful. 3. I was tired. I went to bed early.
Answers
  1. It was raining, so I took an umbrella. 2. I like my job, but it's very stressful.
  2. I went to bed early because I was tired. (or: I was tired, so I went to bed early.)

2. Complete. If the flight is cancelled, ______. / If I had a car, ______.

Sample answers

…I'll book a train ticket. / …I would drive to work.

3. Give your opinion with a reason: "Is working from home better than working in the office?"

docs.title: Speak today
docs.text:
• Use because and so in at least 3 sentences each
  • Give one opinion at work with "I think… because…"
  • Disagree once politely: "I see it a bit differently…"

docs.title: Day 11 · Numbers, Time, Dates & Money
docs.text: Day11Phase 1 · English · Day 11 of 80 Done

docs.title: Numbers, Time, Dates & Money
docs.text: Today's goal: say and understand prices, phone numbers, times, dates and spellings without confusion. You need these at every counter, on every call, and at every station.

docs.title: Big numbers
docs.text:
Number Say it 150 one hundred and fifty 1,250 one thousand two hundred and fifty 15,000 fifteen thousand 1,00,000 (Indian) = 100,000 one lakh = one hundred thousand 10,00,000 = 1,000,000 ten lakh = one million 1,00,00,000 = 10,000,000 one crore = ten million

With international colleagues, convert lakh and crore

"₹25 lakh" → "about 2.5 million rupees" or "around 30,000 US dollars".

Teens vs tens: say them clearly. thirTEEN (13) vs THIRty (30), fifTEEN (15) vs FIFty (50). If unsure, confirm: "One-five or five-zero?"

docs.title: Money
docs.text:
• ₹250 → "two hundred and fifty rupees"
  • ₹99.50 → "ninety-nine rupees fifty (paise)"
  • $4.99 → "four ninety-nine" or "four dollars ninety-nine cents"
  • How much is it? · How much does it cost? · What's the total? · Is that including tax?
  • "That comes to ₹840." · "Here's ₹1,000." · "Your change is ₹160."

docs.title: Phone numbers & codes
docs.text: Say digits one by one, in groups: 98450 12345 → "nine-eight-four-five-oh, one-two-three-four-five". 0 = "zero" or "oh" · 44 = "double four" · 777 = "triple seven". Always read numbers back: "Let me repeat that: nine-eight-four…"

docs.title: Time
docs.text:
Time Say it 7:00 seven o'clock 7:15 seven fifteen / quarter past seven 7:30 seven thirty / half past seven 7:45 seven forty-five / quarter to eight 7:10 seven ten / ten past seven 7:50 seven fifty / ten to eight 19:00 7 pm / seven in the evening

at 6 pm · in the morning / afternoon / evening · at night · around 7 (approximately) · sharp (exactly: "10 o'clock sharp")

docs.title: Dates
docs.text:
• Write: 15 March 2026 / 15/03/2026 (India, UK) · March 15, 2026 / 03/15/2026 (US). In global teams, write the month as a word.
  • Say: "the fifteenth of March" or "March fifteenth".
  • Ordinals: 1st first · 2nd second · 3rd third · 4th fourth · 5th fifth · 21st twenty-first · 22nd twenty-second · 31st thirty-first
  • on Monday / on 5 June · in June / in 2026 · at the weekend (UK) / on the weekend (US)

docs.title: Spelling out loud
docs.text:
Use a word for each letter when the line is bad: A for Apple, B for Bombay, S for Sugar, M for Mumbai, N for Nagpur, P for Pune, D for Delhi…

"My name is Gupta: G for Goa, U for Umbrella, P for Pune, T for Tiger, A for Apple."

docs.title: Conversation: booking a table on the phone
docs.text: RestaurantGood evening, Spice Garden. How can I help you? YouHi, I'd like to book a table for six people on Saturday, the 14th. RestaurantSure. What time? YouAt 8 pm, please. RestaurantLet me check… Yes, that's available. Could I have your name? YouGupta. G for Goa, U for Umbrella, P for Pune, T for Tiger, A for Apple. RestaurantThank you. And a phone number? YouIt's 98450 12345. Restaurant98450 12345? YouThat's right. RestaurantDone. A table for six, Saturday the 14th, at 8 pm. YouPerfect. Is there a minimum charge for groups? RestaurantNo, there isn't. YouGreat, thank you. See you on Saturday!

docs.title: Practice
docs.text:
1. Say these out loud: ₹4,75,000 · 9:45 · 22nd August · 080 2345 6677 · 1.5 crore

Answers

four lakh seventy-five thousand rupees · nine forty-five / quarter to ten · the twenty-second of August · oh-eight-oh, two-three-four-five, six-six-seven-seven (double six, double seven) · one and a half crore (fifteen million)

2. Choose at, on or in: ___ 7 pm · ___ Monday · ___ July · ___ the morning · ___ 25 December

Answers

at · on · in · in · on

3. Spell your full name using a word for each letter, then say your phone number in groups.

docs.text:

  • Spell your name with the "A for Apple" method once
  • Ask "Is that including tax?" or "What's the total?" at a shop

docs.title: Describing People, Places & Problems
docs.text: Today's goal: describe people, places, things and problems clearly, and compare options. You'll use this to report lost items, explain a bug, choose a hotel, or find a person in a crowd.

docs.title: Adjectives: where they go
docs.text:
a / an + adjective + noun · be + adjective
  • a big black suitcase · an old building · a quiet room
  • The room is quiet. · The app is slow. · She looks tired.

Order (when you use several): opinion → size → age → colour → material → noun: "a nice small old red leather bag" (in practice, use 2–3).

docs.title: Describing people
docs.text:
Topic Words Height & build tall, short, average height, slim, well-built Hair short / long, straight / curly, black / grey, bald Age young, middle-aged, elderly, in his thirties Clothes wearing a blue shirt, a red saree, glasses, a cap Personality friendly, helpful, quiet, confident, patient, strict

"He's about 60, short, with grey hair and glasses. He's wearing a white kurta."

docs.title: Describing places and things
docs.text:
• Place: crowded, quiet, clean, noisy, modern, spacious, well-located, far from / close to…
  • Things: heavy, light, broken, new, second-hand, waterproof, made of steel / plastic / cotton
  • Location words: next to, opposite, behind, in front of, between, near, on the corner of

docs.title: Comparing
docs.text:
Short adjectives Long adjectives Irregular cheap → cheaper → the cheapest expensive → more expensive → the most expensive good → better → the best big → bigger → the biggest comfortable → more comfortable bad → worse → the worst easy → easier → the easiest convenient → more convenient far → farther → the farthest
  • The metro is faster than the bus. · This is the cheapest option. · It's not as big as the other room.

docs.title: Describing a problem (any kind)
docs.text:
What's wrong → since when → how bad → what you tried Situation Description Lost bag "It's a medium-sized black backpack with a red keychain. It has my laptop inside." Broken appliance "The washing machine makes a loud noise and doesn't drain. It started yesterday." App bug "The app freezes on the payment screen every time I tap 'Pay'. I've restarted the phone." Health "I've had a sharp pain in my lower back for three days. It's worse in the morning."

Useful problem words: broken, not working, stuck, leaking, cracked, missing, damaged, too loud, too slow, freezing, overheating, keeps (+ -ing): "It keeps crashing."

docs.title: Conversation: lost bag at the metro station
docs.text: YouExcuse me, I think I left my bag on the train. StaffWhich train, and what time? YouThe one that arrived at platform 2 at about 9:15, from Whitefield. StaffCan you describe the bag? YouIt's a medium-sized black backpack. It's quite heavy, and it has a red keychain on the zip. StaffWhat's inside? YouMy laptop, a charger, and a blue water bottle. My office ID card is in the front pocket. StaffOkay. Please fill in this form. We'll check with the last station. YouThank you. How long does it usually take? StaffAbout an hour. Please wait near the customer care counter. YouOkay. Here's my phone number, in case you find it.

docs.title: Practice
docs.text:
1. Compare: cab vs metro (fast, cheap, comfortable).

Sample answer

The metro is cheaper and faster than a cab during rush hour, but a cab is more comfortable.

2. Describe a person you can see right now in 3 sentences (height, hair, clothes).

3. Describe a problem with something at home using: what's wrong → since when → how bad → what you tried.

Sample answer

The kitchen tap is leaking. It started two days ago. It drips all the time, and there's water on the floor. I tightened it, but it didn't help.

docs.text:

  • Compare two options using -er than / more … than
  • Describe one problem clearly (at home, at work, or with an app)

docs.title: Day 13 · Common Mistakes & Fixes
docs.text: Day13Phase 1 · English · Day 13 of 80 Done

docs.title: Common Mistakes & Fixes
docs.text: Today's goal: fix the mistakes that many Indian English speakers make. You'll recognise most of them. Fixing just these makes your English sound much clearer and more natural.

docs.title: Articles: a, an, the
docs.text:
Rule ✅ Example a before a consonant sound a bank, a user, a university (sounds like "you") an before a vowel sound an app, an hour (silent h), an MBA ("em") the when both people know which one Please close the door. · The meeting is at 3. No article for general plurals / uncountables Developers like coffee. · I need information. Places of routine (no "the") go to work / school / bed / college "the" for unique things the sun, the internet, the CEO

❌ I am going to office. → ✅ I'm going to the office. (or "going to work")

docs.title: Prepositions
docs.text: ❌ Common mistake ✅ Correct discuss about the plan discuss the plan (no "about") reach to office reach the office / get to the office married with her married to her good in English good at English angry on me angry with me wait for 5 minutes ✔ / wait me wait for me on the weekend / at the weekend ✔ on Monday, in May, at 6 pm He is in leave He's on leave I live here since 5 years I've lived here for 5 years / since 2021

docs.title: Tenses & verbs
docs.text: ❌ Mistake ✅ Fix Rule I am having two kids. I have two kids. "have" for owning isn't -ing I am knowing him. I know him. state verbs: know, understand, want, like I have seen him yesterday. I saw him yesterday. finished time → past simple He don't know. He doesn't know. he/she/it → doesn't Did you went? Did you go? did + base verb I am working here since 2020. I've been working here since 2020. since/for → present perfect Myself Ashish. I'm Ashish. / My name is Ashish. "myself" isn't used to introduce

docs.title: Indian English that confuses global listeners
docs.text: Instead of Say Do the needful Could you please [specific action]? I have a doubt I have a question Revert back Reply / Get back to me Prepone Move earlier / Bring forward Out of station Travelling / Out of town Today itself / Now itself Today / Right now Pass out (from college) Graduate Updation Update Kindly do it fast Could you please do it soon? Only (at the end: "I told you only") I told you. / I told you already. Is it? (as reaction) Really? / Oh, is that right?

docs.title: Pronunciation hotspots
docs.text:
• v and w: very (teeth on lip) vs west (round lips)
  • th: think (tongue between teeth), not "tink"
  • Stress: DEVeloper, deVELop, COMpany, ANalyst, hoTEL, CALendar
  • Don't add a vowel before s + consonant: "school" not "is-school", "station" not "is-station"

docs.title: Conversation: a quick self-check
docs.text: ColleagueDid you discuss the release plan with the client? YouYes, I discussed the plan with them this morning. ColleagueAnd when is the release? YouThey want to bring it forward by a week, to the 10th. ColleagueOh! Is Ravi available? I heard he's on leave. YouHe's on leave until Wednesday, but he'll reply to emails. ColleagueOkay. I have a question about the test environment, actually. YouSure. I've been working on it since Monday, so I can help.

docs.title: Practice
docs.text:
Fix all the mistakes.

  1. Myself Priya, I am working in TCS since 4 years.
  2. Please do the needful and revert back today itself.
  3. I have a doubt, we can discuss about it tomorrow?
  4. He is in leave, he will reach to office on Monday.
  5. I am having an Honda bike.
Answers
  1. I'm Priya. I've been working at TCS for four years.
  2. Could you please approve it and reply today?
  3. I have a question. Can we discuss it tomorrow?
  4. He's on leave. He'll get to the office on Monday.
  5. I have a Honda bike. (H in "Honda" is pronounced, so "a")

docs.title: Speak today
docs.text:
• Choose 3 mistakes from this page that you make, and write them on a sticky note
  • Catch yourself once today and correct it out loud
  • Ask the AI tutor: "Track my mistakes from this list in every lesson"

Phase 1 complete!

You can now build sentences, ask and answer any question, use the past and future, and speak politely. Tomorrow starts Phase 2: Communication & Confidence.

docs.title: Day 22 · Airport
docs.text: Day22Phase 3 · Everyday Life · Day 22 of 80 Done

docs.title: At the Airport
docs.text: An airport is a series of short conversations with people who are busy. Have your documents ready, answer exactly what's asked, and don't be shy about asking for help.

docs.title: Your airport journey
docs.text: 1. Check-in & bag drop 2. Security screening 3. Immigration / passport control — international 4. Gate & boarding 5. On the plane 6. Arrival: immigration, baggage, customs

docs.title: 1. Check-in counter
docs.text:
What you'll be askedWhat you can ask They ask You answer "May I see your passport / ID and ticket, please?" "Sure, here you go." "Where are you flying to today?" "To Singapore, then connecting to Sydney." "How many bags are you checking in?" "Just one, and one cabin bag." "Did you pack your bags yourself?" "Yes, I did." "Are you carrying any batteries, power banks, or liquids in your checked bag?" "No, the power bank is in my cabin bag." "Window or aisle?" "Aisle, please." "Your bag is 3 kg over. There's an excess charge." "Could I move some items to my cabin bag instead?"
  • "Could I get an aisle / window seat, please?"
  • "Is it possible to sit together with my colleague?"
  • "Is my bag checked through to my final destination, or do I collect it in transit?"
  • "What time does boarding start, and which gate?"
  • "Is there any extra legroom / exit row seat available?"
  • "What's the baggage allowance on this ticket?"
  • "Can I add my frequent flyer number?"
  • "Is the flight on time?"

docs.title: 2. Security
docs.text:
You'll hear Meaning / what to do "Laptops and liquids out, please." Put laptop & liquids (≤100 ml, in a clear bag) in a separate tray "Anything in your pockets?" Wallet, phone, keys, coins go in the tray "Please remove your belt / shoes / jacket." Do it, place in tray "Step through, please. Arms up." Walk through the scanner / body scanner "Is this your bag? I need to check it." "Yes, sure, go ahead." Stay calm. Random checks are normal.

You can ask: "Do I need to take out my tablet / charger too?" · "Can I keep my shoes on?"

docs.title: 3. Immigration (international)
docs.text:
Golden rule

Answer only what's asked, honestly, briefly. Keep documents ready: passport, visa, return ticket, hotel booking, invitation letter.

Officer asks Good answer "What's the purpose of your visit?" "Business. I'm attending a tech conference." / "Tourism." "How long will you stay?" "Five days. I return on the 12th." "Where will you be staying?" "At the Marina Hotel, here's the booking." "Who is your employer / what do you do?" "I'm a senior software engineer at XYZ Technologies." "Have you been here before?" "Yes, once in 2024." / "No, first time." "Are you carrying more than [X] in cash?" "No." / "Yes, here's my declaration." "Do you have a return ticket?" "Yes, here it is."

If you don't understand: "Sorry, could you repeat that, please?" Don't guess.

docs.title: 4. At the gate & boarding
docs.text:
You can ask:

  • "Excuse me, is this the gate for the Mumbai flight?"
  • "Has boarding started for AI 302?"
  • "Is the flight delayed? Do you know the new time?"
  • "Which boarding group am I in?"
  • "Can I take this bag on board, or does it need to be gate-checked?"

Announcements decoded:

Announcement Meaning "Pre-boarding for families and passengers needing assistance" Not you yet (unless it applies) "Now boarding zones 1 and 2" Check your boarding pass zone/group "Final call for passenger…" Hurry! The gate is closing "Gate change" Check the screens, move to the new gate

docs.title: 5. On the plane
docs.text:
• "Excuse me, I think you're in my seat. I'm 14C." (show boarding pass, smile)
  • "Could you help me put my bag in the overhead bin?"
  • "Could I have a glass of water, please?"
  • "Is it possible to change seats? There's an empty one at the back."
  • "Excuse me, could I get past? Thank you."
  • "What time do we land (local time)?"

docs.title: 6. Arrival
docs.text:
BaggageLost / damaged bagCustoms
  • "Which belt is the bag from flight SQ 421 on?"
  • "Where is the baggage services / lost & found desk?"

"Hi, my bag didn't arrive on flight SQ 421 from Bangalore. Here's my baggage tag. It's a large black suitcase with a red ribbon. Could you file a report? When can I expect it, and can it be delivered to my hotel? Is there an allowance for essentials meanwhile?"

Always get a reference number (PIR) and a phone/email for follow-up.

Asked Answer "Anything to declare?" "No, nothing." / "Yes, I have [item]." "Are you carrying food items?" Be honest: "Yes, some packaged snacks."

docs.title: When things go wrong
docs.text:
Flight delayed / cancelledMissed connectionCan't find your gate / lost

"My flight to Delhi has been cancelled. What are my options? Can you rebook me on the next available flight? Will the airline provide a hotel / meal voucher? And can I get that in writing?"

"My first flight was delayed and I missed my connection to London. Here's my boarding pass. Can you put me on the next flight? Will my checked bag be transferred too?"

"Excuse me, I'm a bit lost. How do I get to the international transfers / Gate B12? Is it a long walk, or should I take the train?"

docs.title: Vocabulary
docs.text: Word Meaning Layover / Stopover A stop between flights (short / long) Transit / Transfer Changing planes Boarding pass The pass that lets you board Carry-on / Cabin bag Bag you take on the plane Checked baggage Bag that goes in the hold Excess baggage Weight over the allowance (fee) Departures / Arrivals Leaving / coming areas Duty-free Tax-free shops after security Jet lag Tiredness from time-zone change Red-eye Overnight flight

docs.title: Check-in with extra baggage
docs.text: StaffGood morning. Passport and ticket, please. YouGood morning. Here you are. I'm flying to Dubai. StaffHow many bags are you checking in? YouTwo bags. StaffYour allowance is 30 kilos. Together they're 34 kilos. YouOh. Can I move some things to my cabin bag? StaffSure, you can use the side area. Five minutes later YouI've moved some clothes. Could you weigh them again? Staff29.5 kilos. Perfect. Window or aisle? YouAisle, please. And could you add my frequent flyer number? StaffDone. Boarding is at 9:10 from gate 24. YouThank you!

docs.title: Flight delay at the gate
docs.text: YouExcuse me, the board says the Delhi flight is delayed. Do you know the new time? StaffYes, it's now 4:30 instead of 2:45. There's a technical issue. YouI have a connecting flight in Delhi at 7. Will I make it? StaffIt will be tight. Let me check if we can protect you on the 9 pm connection. YouThank you. Will my bag also be moved? StaffYes, it's checked through. Here's a meal voucher for the delay. YouThanks. Could you write the new connection details on my boarding pass?

docs.title: Day 31 · Bank & Money
docs.text: Day31Phase 3 · Everyday Life · Day 31 of 80 Done

docs.title: Bank & Shopping
docs.text: When money is involved, be clear, confirm details, and get it in writing.

docs.title: At the bank
docs.text:
Need Say Open an account "I'd like to open a savings account. What documents do I need?" Card blocked "My card has been blocked after a failed transaction. Could you help me unblock it?" Wrong charge "There's a transaction I don't recognise: ₹4,500 on the 2nd. I'd like to raise a dispute." Transfer "I need to make an international transfer. What are the charges and exchange rate?" Loan "What's the interest rate for a home loan, and is it fixed or floating?" Fees "Are there any hidden charges or minimum balance requirements?"

Tip

Always ask: "Could I get a reference number for this request?" and "How long will it take?"

docs.title: Shopping
docs.text:
• "I'm just looking, thanks."
  • "Do you have this in a bigger / smaller size? In blue?"
  • "Can I try this on? Where's the fitting room?"
  • "Is there a discount on this?" / "Is this the final price?"
  • "What's the return / exchange policy?"
  • "Does it come with a warranty?"

docs.title: Returns & complaints
docs.text:
"Hi, I bought these headphones last week and the left side stopped working. Here's the receipt. I'd like a replacement or a refund, please."

If it's not resolved: "Could I speak to the manager, please?" Stay calm and polite, and repeat the facts.

docs.title: Bargaining (local markets)
docs.text:
1. "How much is this?"
  2. "Hmm, that's a bit much. Could you do ₹400?"
  3. "If I buy two, what's your best price?"
  4. Smile and walk away politely if it's too high: "Thanks, I'll think about it."

docs.title: Opening an account
docs.text: OfficerGood morning. How can I help you? YouGood morning. I'd like to open a savings account. OfficerSure. Do you have your Aadhaar and PAN cards? YouYes, here they are. What's the minimum balance? Officer₹10,000 for this account. There's also a zero-balance salary account if your company has a tie-up. YouLet me check with HR. Is there a debit card fee? OfficerThe first year is free. After that, ₹299 a year. YouOkay. How long will it take to open the account? OfficerTwo working days. You'll get the details by SMS. YouThank you. I'll fill in the form now.

docs.title: Disputing a transaction
docs.text: YouHi, there's a transaction on my card that I don't recognise. OfficerI'm sorry. Could you tell me the date and amount? You₹4,500 on the 2nd, from an online store I've never used. OfficerLet me block your card first for safety. YouYes, please. And I'd like to raise a dispute. OfficerI've raised it. Your reference number is DSP-22081. It takes up to 45 days. YouWill I get a temporary credit in the meantime? OfficerYes, within 10 working days. YouThank you. When will I get a new card? OfficerIn about a week, by courier.

docs.title: Day 32 · Bank Locker
docs.text: Day32Phase 3 · Everyday Life · Day 32 of 80 Done

docs.title: Bank Locker
docs.text:
Today's goal: apply for a bank locker, ask about rent, rules and access, operate it with a joint holder, and handle problems like a lost key or surrendering the locker.

Rules differ by bank

Locker rent, deposits, access rules and agreements depend on your bank and country. Always ask for the written agreement and read it before signing.

docs.title: Key words
docs.text: Word / phrase Meaning safe deposit locker a locked box in the bank's vault small / medium / large locker sizes (rent depends on size) annual rent / advance rent yearly fee fixed deposit (FD) as security some banks ask for an FD locker agreement the contract with the bank waiting list queue when no locker is free joint holder / operate jointly / either or survivor two people can use it nominee / nomination who gets access if the holder dies access / operation / visit opening the locker locker key / master key your key / the bank's key (both needed) surrender / break open give it back / force it open (for example, if the key is lost)

docs.title: Questions you'll ask
docs.text:
ApplyingUsing it
  • Is a locker available at this branch? What sizes?
  • What's the annual rent for a medium locker?
  • Do I need a fixed deposit or a savings account here?
  • Is there a waiting list? How long is it?
  • What documents do I need?
  • Can I add my wife as a joint holder? And a nominee?
  • Could I read the locker agreement before I sign?
  • What are the locker operating hours?
  • How many visits are free each year?
  • Do I need to book a visit in advance?
  • Can my joint holder visit alone?
  • What is not allowed inside the locker?
  • What's the bank's liability if something is lost or damaged?

docs.title: Conversation 1: applying for a locker
docs.text: YouGood morning. I'd like to apply for a locker at this branch. OfficerGood morning. Do you have an account with us? YouYes, a savings account. Here's my account number. OfficerThank you. We have medium lockers available. Small ones have a waiting list. YouWhat's the annual rent for a medium locker? Officer₹4,000 plus GST, paid in advance. YouDo I need a fixed deposit as well? OfficerYes, an FD covering three years' rent, as security. YouOkay. Can my wife be a joint holder, and can I add a nominee? OfficerYes, both. Please fill in this form, and bring her ID and photographs. YouCould I take a copy of the locker agreement to read first? OfficerOf course. Here it is. YouThank you. I'll bring everything tomorrow.

docs.title: Conversation 2: lost locker key
docs.text: YouHi. I'm afraid I've lost my locker key. The locker number is 214. OfficerI'm sorry to hear that. When did you last use it? YouAbout two months ago. I've searched the whole house, but I can't find it. OfficerYou'll need to give a written request and an indemnity, and possibly a police report. YouOkay. What happens next? OfficerWe'll arrange for the locker to be opened in your presence by the vendor, and the lock will be changed. YouIs there a charge for that? OfficerYes, the charges for breaking it open and replacing the lock. About ₹5,000. YouUnderstood. How long will it take? OfficerAbout a week. We'll call you with a date. YouThank you. Could you give me the list of documents I need to submit?

docs.title: Other useful sentences
docs.text:
• "I'd like to operate my locker, number 214."
  • "I'd like to surrender my locker. What's the process for the FD and the key?"
  • "I haven't received the rent debit notice. Has it been paid?"
  • "Could you update the nominee on my locker?"

docs.title: Practice
docs.text:
Write 5 questions you would ask before signing a locker agreement.

Sample answers

What's the annual rent, and can it increase? · Is an FD required? · How many free visits are there each year? · What happens if I lose the key? · What is the bank's liability if something is damaged?

docs.text:

  • Learn the difference between joint holder and nominee

docs.title: Day 24 · Cab, Auto & Directions
docs.text: Day24Phase 3 · Everyday Life · Day 24 of 80 Done

docs.title: Cab & Directions
docs.text: Confirm, clarify, stay safe. Short, clear phrases work best with drivers and strangers.

docs.title: Booking / starting a ride
docs.text:
• "Hi, are you here for Ashish? Going to Terminal 2?" (confirm the driver before you get in)
  • "Can you follow the map, please?"
  • "How long will it take with this traffic?"
  • "Could you turn the AC up / down, please?"
  • "Could you stop here, please? Just after the signal."
  • "Could you wait 5 minutes? I need to pick up a bag."

docs.title: Taxi without an app (fixed fare)
docs.text:
• "How much to the railway station?"
  • "Do you use the meter?"
  • "That seems high. Could you do ₹300?"

docs.title: Asking for directions
docs.text:
"Excuse me, sorry to bother you. How do I get to the Central Library? Is it walking distance?"

Ask Useful when "Is it far from here?" Deciding walk vs cab "Which way is the metro station?" Need a direction "Is there a bus that goes there?" Public transport "Can you show me on the map?" Directions are complicated "So, straight, then left at the bank. Right?" Confirming (repeat back!)

Direction vocabulary: go straight · turn left/right · take the second left · at the signal/roundabout · opposite · next to · around the corner · cross the road.

docs.title: Safety phrases
docs.text:
• "Please don't take a different route without asking me."
  • "I'm sharing my live location with my family."
  • "Please stop the car. I'd like to get out here."

docs.title: Talking to the cab driver
docs.text: DriverHello, Ashish sir? YouYes. Are you going to Terminal 2, Kempegowda Airport? DriverYes, please sit. YouCould you follow the map, please? There's usually traffic at Hebbal. DriverOkay. Should I take the toll road? YouYes, that's fine. I'll pay the toll. How long will it take? DriverAbout 55 minutes. YouMy flight is at 9:30. Could you please drive a bit faster, but safely? DriverDon't worry, we'll reach by 8:15. YouThank you. Could you turn the AC down a little?

docs.title: Asking a stranger for directions
docs.text: YouExcuse me, sorry to bother you. Do you know where the City Library is? StrangerYes, it's not far. Go straight for about 200 metres. YouOkay, straight. StrangerAt the traffic signal, turn left. It's the second building on your right, opposite the bank. YouSo, straight, left at the signal, and it's on the right, opposite the bank? StrangerExactly. It's about five minutes on foot. YouThank you so much! StrangerYou're welcome.

docs.title: Day 49 · Invitations & Celebrations
docs.text: Day49Phase 3 · Everyday Life · Day 49 of 80 Done

docs.title: Invitations & Celebrations
docs.text: Today's goal: invite people, accept or decline, give wishes for birthdays, weddings and festivals, and make conversation at celebrations.

docs.title: Inviting
docs.text:
• "We're having a small get-together on Saturday evening. Would you like to come?"
  • "It's my daughter's birthday on the 12th. We'd love it if you could join us."
  • "You're invited to our housewarming on Sunday, 1 pm onwards."
  • "Are you free for dinner next Friday?"

docs.title: Accepting & declining
docs.text: Accept Decline politely I'd love to! What time? Thank you so much for inviting me. Unfortunately, I'm travelling that weekend. Sounds great. Can I bring anything? I'm so sorry, I have a prior commitment. Let's catch up soon! Count me in! I'd love to, but I can't make it this time. Have a wonderful evening! Thank you, we'll definitely be there. I might be a little late. Is that okay?

docs.title: Wishes for every occasion
docs.text: Occasion What to say Birthday Happy birthday! Wishing you a wonderful year ahead. Wedding Congratulations! Wishing you both a lifetime of happiness. Anniversary Happy anniversary! Here's to many more years together. New baby Congratulations on the little one! How are mother and baby doing? New job / promotion Congratulations! You really deserve it. Festival Happy Diwali! / Eid Mubarak! / Merry Christmas! / Happy Pongal! Wishing you and your family joy and prosperity. Housewarming Congratulations on the new home! It looks beautiful. Condolence I'm so sorry for your loss. Please let me know if there's anything I can do. Get well Get well soon! Take care and rest well.

docs.title: Conversation 1: inviting a colleague
docs.text: YouHey Meena, are you free on Sunday evening? MeenaI think so. Why? YouWe're having a housewarming party at our new flat. We'd love it if you could come. MeenaCongratulations on the new place! I'd love to. What time? YouAnytime after 6. I'll send you the location. MeenaGreat. Can I bring anything? YouJust yourself! And your husband, of course. MeenaThank you. We'll be there.

docs.title: Conversation 2: at a wedding reception
docs.text: YouCongratulations, Rahul! You look great. And congratulations, Divya! RahulThank you so much for coming! Divya, this is Ashish, my colleague from Bengaluru. DivyaNice to meet you! Thank you for travelling all this way. YouIt's a pleasure. The decorations are beautiful. Wishing you both a lifetime of happiness. DivyaThank you! Please have dinner before you leave. YouDefinitely. Rahul, the photos from the sangeet looked amazing. RahulYou should have come! Next time, no excuses. YouHa, I promise. Enjoy your evening!

docs.title: Small talk at parties
docs.text:
• "How do you know the host?"
  • "The food is amazing. Have you tried the desserts?"
  • "Did you travel far to get here?"
  • "It was lovely meeting you. I hope to see you again soon."

docs.title: Speak today
docs.text:
• Send one invitation or wish in English (WhatsApp counts)
  • Practise declining politely with "Thank you so much… unfortunately…"

docs.title: Practise with AI

docs.title: Day 45 · Customer Care & Complaints
docs.text: Day45Phase 3 · Everyday Life · Day 45 of 80 Done

docs.title: Customer Care & Complaints
docs.text: Today's goal: call or chat with customer care for mobile, internet, apps and services, explain the issue fast, stay calm, escalate politely, and get a complaint number.

docs.title: Key words
docs.text: Word / phrase Meaning customer care / support / helpline the service team complaint / ticket / reference number the record of your issue escalate / supervisor / nodal officer take it to a higher level recharge / plan / postpaid / prepaid mobile plans network issue / no signal / slow speed / outage connection problems technician visit someone comes to your home refund / reversal / chargeback money back TAT (turnaround time) how long they'll take

docs.title: The complaint formula
docs.text:
Who you are → what's wrong → since when → what you tried → what you want

"Hi, my name is Ashish Gupta, and my account number is 7781 2345. My home internet hasn't been working since yesterday evening. The router shows a red light. I've restarted it twice. I'd like a technician visit today, please."

docs.title: Questions you'll ask
docs.text:
• Could I have the complaint number, please?
  • How long will it take to fix? / What's the TAT?
  • Will I get a credit for the days the service didn't work?
  • Could you escalate this, please? / Could I speak to your supervisor?
  • Can you send me the details by email/SMS?
  • Why was I charged ₹499 extra this month?

docs.title: Conversation 1: internet down
docs.text: AgentThank you for calling FastNet. My name is Rohit. How may I help you? YouHi Rohit. My home internet has been down since 8 pm yesterday. The account is in the name of Ashish Gupta. AgentMay I have your registered mobile number? YouIt's 98450 12345. AgentThank you. Have you tried restarting the router? YouYes, twice. The "internet" light is red. AgentI can see an outage in your area. It should be fixed in four hours. YouI work from home, so this is urgent. Could you give me a complaint number? AgentSure, it's FN-552190. YouThank you. Will I get a credit for the downtime? AgentYes, the credit will be added automatically to your next bill. YouGreat. If it isn't fixed by 2 pm, I'll call back with this number.

docs.title: Conversation 2: escalating a wrong charge
docs.text: YouHi, I called twice about a wrong charge of ₹1,200 on my bill, but it hasn't been fixed. AgentI'm sorry. Could you share the complaint number? YouIt's MB-81234. I was charged for international roaming, but I haven't travelled abroad. AgentI can see the complaint. It's still under review. YouIt's been ten days. I'd like this escalated, please. Could I speak to a supervisor? AgentPlease hold, I'll transfer you. SupervisorHello, I'm Anjali, the supervisor. I've checked: the charge was a system error. YouThank you. When will the amount be reversed? SupervisorWithin 48 hours. You'll get an SMS confirmation. YouCould you also confirm it by email, please? SupervisorYes, I'll send it now.

docs.title: Staying calm (and effective)
docs.text: ❌ Avoid ✅ Try Shouting at the agent "I know it's not your fault. I just need this fixed today." Explaining the whole story again "Here's my complaint number, and here's what's still pending." Ending the call without a number "Before we finish, could I have the reference number?"

docs.title: Practice
docs.text: Write your own complaint using the formula for a real or imagined problem (phone, app, delivery, bank).

docs.text:

docs.title: Key words
docs.text: Dentist Eye clinic toothache / sensitivity / cavity blurry / blurred vision, eye strain filling / root canal / extraction eye test / power / prescription cleaning / scaling glasses / spectacles / frames / lenses gums (bleeding, swollen) contact lenses / anti-glare coating wisdom tooth / braces / crown dry eyes / itching / redness X-ray / numb / anaesthetic near-sighted (can't see far) / far-sighted

docs.title: Questions you'll ask
docs.text:
DentistEye clinic
  • Can I get an appointment for a check-up this week?
  • Will it hurt? Will you give me an injection?
  • Do I need a root canal, or is a filling enough?
  • How many sittings will it take?
  • How much will it cost? Is it covered by insurance?
  • When can I eat after the treatment?
  • I'd like an eye test. Do I need an appointment?
  • Has my power changed?
  • Do I need to wear glasses all the time, or only for reading / screens?
  • What's the difference between these lenses?
  • How long will the glasses take to be ready?
  • Are these drops safe with contact lenses?

docs.title: Conversation 1: at the dentist
docs.text: DentistWhat seems to be the problem? YouI have pain in a lower back tooth on the right side. It hurts when I drink something cold. DentistHow long has it been like this? YouAbout two weeks. It's getting worse. DentistLet me take a look… There's a deep cavity. We'll take an X-ray to check. YouWill I need a root canal? DentistIf the X-ray shows the nerve is affected, yes. Otherwise, a filling will do. YouHow many sittings does a root canal take, and how much does it cost? DentistUsually two or three sittings. It's about ₹6,000, plus ₹8,000 for the crown. YouOkay. Will it hurt? DentistNo, we'll make the area numb first. You'll only feel some pressure. YouAlright, let's do the X-ray.

docs.title: Conversation 2: eye test and glasses
docs.text: OptometristPlease read the smallest line you can see. YouE, F, P… sorry, the next line is blurry. OptometristOkay. Do you find it hard to see far away, or close up? YouFar away. Road signs are blurry when I drive at night. And my eyes get tired after work. OptometristYour power has increased slightly, to minus 1.5 in both eyes. YouDo I need to wear glasses all the time? OptometristFor driving and screens, yes. I'd suggest lenses with a blue-light filter. YouHow much do they cost, and when will they be ready? Optometrist₹3,500 for the lenses, plus the frame. They'll be ready in three days. YouCan I also get a copy of the prescription? OptometristOf course.

docs.title: Practice
docs.text:
Describe a health problem using: where it hurts + what kind of pain + since when + what makes it worse.

Sample answer

I have a sharp pain in my upper left tooth since Monday. It's worse when I eat something sweet.

docs.title: Day 36 · Doctor & Pharmacy
docs.text: Day36Phase 3 · Everyday Life · Day 36 of 80 Done

docs.title: Doctor & Pharmacy
docs.text: Being precise with a doctor is like writing a good bug report: symptoms, when it started, how bad it is, and what makes it better or worse.

docs.title: The "health bug report"
docs.text:
What:      sore throat and fever (101°F)
Since:     2 days, started Tuesday night
Severity:  pain 6/10 when swallowing
Pattern:   worse at night
Tried:     paracetamol — helps for ~4 hours
Other:     no allergies; I take blood-pressure medicine (amlodipine)

docs.title: At the doctor's
docs.text:
Describing symptoms:

  • "I've had a headache for three days."
  • "It's a sharp / dull / throbbing / burning pain."
  • "It hurts when I bend down / swallow / breathe deeply."
  • "I feel dizzy / nauseous / tired all the time."
  • "I'm allergic to penicillin."

Questions to ask the doctor:

  • "What do you think is causing this?"
  • "Is it serious? Is it contagious?"
  • "How often should I take this medicine, and for how long?"
  • "Are there any side effects I should watch for?"
  • "Can I work / travel / exercise?"
  • "When should I come back if it doesn't get better?"
  • "Do I need any tests?"

docs.title: At the pharmacy
docs.text:
• "I have a prescription for this."
  • "Do you have something for a cough / cold / acidity?"
  • "Is this safe to take with my blood-pressure medicine?"
  • "Should I take it before or after food?"
  • "Is there a generic / cheaper version?"

docs.title: Emergencies
docs.text:
Emergency phrases

"I need an ambulance. Someone has collapsed at [exact address / landmark]." "Please call a doctor, it's urgent." "Where is the nearest hospital / emergency room?"

India: 112 (all emergencies) · 108 (ambulance in many states). Abroad: learn the local emergency number before you travel (e.g. 911 US, 112 EU, 999 UK).

docs.title: At the doctor's
docs.text: DoctorGood morning. What brings you here today? YouGood morning, doctor. I've had a sore throat and a fever for two days. DoctorHow high is the fever? YouIt was 101 last night. I took a paracetamol, and it came down for a few hours. DoctorAny cough or body pain? YouA dry cough, and some body ache. DoctorLet me check your throat… It's an infection. I'll prescribe an antibiotic for five days. YouShould I take it before or after food? DoctorAfter food, twice a day. Drink warm water and rest. YouCan I go to work? DoctorRest for two days. Come back if the fever doesn't go down by Friday. YouThank you, doctor.

docs.title: At the pharmacy
docs.text: YouHi, I have a prescription for these medicines. PharmacistLet me see… We have both. Do you want the full course of the antibiotic? YouYes, the full five days. Is there a generic version of the cough syrup? PharmacistYes, it's cheaper and works the same way. YouOkay, I'll take that. Can I take the syrup with the antibiotic? PharmacistYes, that's fine. Just keep two hours between the syrup and any antacid. YouThank you. Could I have a bill for insurance? PharmacistSure, here it is.
