docs.title: Key words
docs.text: Word / phrase Meaning cabin crew / flight attendant staff on the plane overhead bin / locker storage above seats aisle / window / middle seat seat positions seat belt sign light that says: stay seated, belt on turbulence bumpy air connecting flight / connection your next flight transit / transfer desk help desk for connections landing card / arrival form form for immigration baggage claim / carousel / belt where bags arrive customs / declare check of goods / tell officials what you're carrying

docs.title: Questions you'll ask (on board)
docs.text:
• Excuse me, I think you're in my seat. I'm in 14C.
  • Could you help me put my bag in the overhead bin?
  • Is it possible to change seats? There's an empty one in row 20.
  • Could I have some water / a blanket / a vegetarian meal?
  • What time do we land, local time?
  • Will I make my connection? I only have 50 minutes.
  • Which gate does my connecting flight leave from?
  • Do I need to collect my bag before my connecting flight?

docs.title: Questions you'll be asked
docs.text: Crew / officer asks You answer Chicken or vegetarian? Vegetarian, please. Something to drink? Just water, please. / Tea with milk, no sugar. Could you put your seat upright / open the window shade? Sure, sorry. Purpose of your visit? (immigration) Business. I'm attending a meeting at our office here. How long are you staying? Six days. I fly back on the 18th. Anything to declare? (customs) No, nothing. / Yes, I have some sweets for my family.

docs.title: Conversation 1: on board
docs.text: YouExcuse me, I think you're sitting in my seat. I'm in 22A, the window. PassengerOh, sorry! I thought this was 21. Let me move. YouNo problem. Thank you. CrewGood evening. Could you put your bag under the seat in front, please? The bins are full. YouSure. Could I have a blanket, please? It's a bit cold. CrewOf course, I'll bring one. YouThanks. And do you know what time we land in Singapore? CrewAt 6:40 local time. That's about 20 minutes early. YouGreat. I have a connecting flight to Sydney. Do I need to collect my bag? CrewIf it's on the same ticket, no. It's checked through. The transfer desk can confirm. YouThank you very much.

docs.title: Conversation 2: immigration on arrival
docs.text: OfficerGood morning. Passport, please. YouGood morning. Here you are. OfficerWhat's the purpose of your visit? YouBusiness. I'm attending a training at our Sydney office. OfficerHow long will you stay? YouSeven days. My return flight is on the 22nd. OfficerWhere are you staying? YouAt the Harbour View Hotel. Here's the booking. OfficerIs this your first visit to Australia? YouYes, it is. OfficerAre you carrying any food? YouYes, some packaged snacks. I've declared them on the form. OfficerOkay. Enjoy your stay. YouThank you.

docs.title: When things go wrong
docs.text:
• "My flight was delayed and I've missed my connection. Can you rebook me?"
  • "My bag hasn't arrived. Here's my baggage tag. Where do I report it?"
  • "My bag is damaged: the handle is broken. I'd like to file a report."
  • "I feel unwell. Could I have some water? Do you have anything for nausea?"
  • "Sorry, I didn't understand the question. Could you repeat it, please?"

docs.title: Practice
docs.text:
Answer the immigration officer in one clear sentence each: purpose, length of stay, where you're staying, your job.

Sample answers

I'm here on holiday. · For ten days. · At my sister's house in Melbourne; here's the address. · I'm a software engineer.

docs.title: Conversation 1: at the passport office
docs.text: OfficerToken number? YouA-142. I'm here for a passport renewal. Here's my appointment letter. OfficerOld passport and documents, please. YouHere's the old passport, my Aadhaar card, and the address proof. OfficerYour address is different from the old passport. YouYes, I've moved to Bengaluru. Here's the rental agreement and an electricity bill. OfficerThe electricity bill is in the owner's name. Do you have anything in your name? YouI have my bank statement with this address. Will that work? OfficerYes, that's fine. Please go to counter B for photos and fingerprints. YouThank you. How long will it take to get the passport? OfficerAfter police verification, about two to three weeks. YouHow can I check the status? OfficerOnline, with your file number. It's on this receipt.

docs.title: Conversation 2: following up by phone
docs.text: YouGood morning. I applied for a driving licence renewal a month ago, but the status still says "under process". ClerkWhat's your application number? YouDL-RN-554210. ClerkLet me check… It's waiting for the officer's approval. YouIs there anything missing from my side? ClerkNo, the documents are complete. YouCould you tell me roughly when it will be approved? ClerkWithin ten working days. YouThank you. If there's no update by then, who should I contact? ClerkYou can email the RTO helpdesk with your application number.

docs.title: Tips
docs.text:
• Carry originals + two photocopies of everything, and passport-size photos.

JoiningWith the trainerOn the gym floor

docs.title: Conversation 1: joining the gym
docs.text: ReceptionistHi! Welcome to FitZone. How can I help you? YouHi. I'd like to join the gym. What plans do you have? ReceptionistMonthly is ₹2,000, quarterly is ₹5,000, and annual is ₹15,000. YouIs there a joining fee? ReceptionistNot this month. We have an offer. YouDoes it include a trainer? ReceptionistA general trainer is included. A personal trainer is ₹6,000 extra per month. YouOkay. Can I try one free session before I decide? ReceptionistSure, come tomorrow at 7 am. Bring sports shoes and a towel. YouGreat. What are the timings on Sundays? Receptionist7 am to 12 noon. YouPerfect. See you tomorrow.

docs.title: Conversation 2: first session with the trainer
docs.text: TrainerSo, what's your goal? YouI want to lose about eight kilos and get fitter. I sit at a desk all day. TrainerGot it. Any injuries or health problems? YouI have some lower back pain sometimes, and I'm a bit stiff. TrainerOkay, we'll avoid heavy deadlifts for now. We'll start with a 10-minute warm-up on the treadmill. YouHow many days a week should I come? TrainerFour days to start: two days strength, two days cardio. Later TrainerNow, three sets of twelve on the leg press. YouIs my form correct? I feel it in my knees. TrainerKeep your feet a little higher, and don't lock your knees. Yes, that's better. YouThanks. Should I stretch after this? TrainerYes, always cool down and stretch for five minutes.

docs.title: Gym etiquette phrases
docs.text:
• "Mind if I use this bench while you rest?"

docs.title: Home Repairs & Services
docs.text: Today's goal: explain a problem to a plumber, electrician or technician, agree on the cost before work starts, and give clear instructions to house help.

docs.title: Key words
docs.text: Word / phrase Meaning leak / drip / blocked / clogged water problems short circuit / tripped / no power / spark electrical problems geyser / water heater / RO / purifier appliances service / repair / replace / spare part the work visiting charge / labour charge fee for coming / for work warranty / AMC (annual maintenance contract) covered repairs house help / cook / driver domestic staff

docs.title: Describing the problem
docs.text:
What + where + since when + what you've tried
  • "The kitchen tap is leaking. It started yesterday. I tightened it, but it still drips."
  • "The bedroom AC isn't cooling. It turns on, but the air is warm. It was serviced six months ago."
  • "The power trips every time we switch on the geyser."

docs.title: Questions you'll ask
docs.text:
• What's the visiting charge?
  • Can you tell me the total cost before you start?
  • What's the problem? Can it be repaired, or does it need replacing?
  • Is the spare part original? Is there a warranty on the repair?

  • Can you come tomorrow morning between 9 and 11?
  • Can I pay by UPI? Could I have a bill?

docs.title: Conversation 1: booking an AC repair
docs.text: AgentCoolCare service, how can I help? YouHi, my split AC isn't cooling. It runs, but the air is warm. AgentWhich brand and how old is it? YouIt's a Daikin, about three years old. AgentWhen was it last serviced? YouAbout eight months ago. AgentIt may need a gas refill. The visiting charge is ₹399, and that's adjusted in the final bill. YouHow much is a gas refill, roughly? AgentBetween ₹2,500 and ₹3,500, depending on the leak. YouOkay. Can the technician come tomorrow between 10 and 12? AgentYes, I've booked it. The technician will call you before coming. YouThank you.

docs.title: Conversation 2: with the technician
docs.text: TechnicianThe gas is very low. There's a small leak near the pipe joint. YouCan you fix the leak, or will you only refill the gas? TechnicianI'll fix the joint first, then refill. YouWhat will the total cost be? Technician₹3,200, including the visiting charge. YouIs there a warranty on the work? TechnicianThree months on the leak repair. YouOkay, please go ahead. Could you also clean the filters? TechnicianYes, no extra charge. YouGreat. Please send me the bill on WhatsApp after you finish.

docs.title: Hospital
docs.text:
Today's goal: handle the hospital: registration, emergency, describing symptoms, admission, visiting a patient, tests, insurance and billing. (For a clinic visit and medicines, see Doctor & Pharmacy.)

Emergency first

In India, call 112 (all emergencies) or 108 (ambulance in many states). Say: "I need an ambulance at [address + landmark]. A man has collapsed and isn't responding."

docs.title: Key words
docs.text: Word / phrase Meaning reception / registration / OPD front desk / signing up / outpatient department emergency / casualty / ER for urgent cases ward / ICU / room where admitted patients stay admit / discharge keep in hospital / allow to go home consultant / specialist / resident doctor types of doctors blood test / X-ray / scan / report tests and results cashless / reimbursement / TPA insurance: hospital bills the insurer / you claim later / insurance desk visiting hours / attendant pass when visitors are allowed / pass for the person staying

docs.title: Questions you'll ask
docs.text:
• Where is the registration counter / emergency?
  • Which doctor should I see for back pain?
  • How long is the waiting time?
  • Is this hospital cashless for [insurance company]?
  • When will the reports be ready?
  • What are the visiting hours? Can I stay overnight?
  • What is the estimated cost of the treatment / surgery?
  • When can he be discharged?
  • Could you explain the report in simple words?

docs.title: Questions you'll be asked
docs.text: They ask You answer Patient's name and age? Ramesh Gupta, 64. What's the problem? He has chest pain and difficulty breathing since this morning. Any existing conditions? Yes, diabetes and high blood pressure. Is he on any medication? Yes, metformin and amlodipine. Any allergies? He's allergic to penicillin. Do you have insurance? Yes, here's the card. Is it cashless here? Who is the attendant? I am, his son.

docs.title: Conversation 1: at the emergency desk
docs.text: YouPlease help. My father has chest pain and he's sweating a lot. NurseOkay, bring him here. What's his name and age? YouRamesh Gupta. He's 64. NurseWhen did the pain start? YouAbout forty minutes ago. It's spreading to his left arm. NurseDoes he have any medical conditions? YouDiabetes and high blood pressure. He takes metformin and amlodipine. NurseAny allergies? YouYes, penicillin. NurseOkay. The doctor will see him right now. Please complete the registration at the counter. YouThank you. Do you need his insurance card? NurseYes, give it to the insurance desk after registration.

docs.title: Conversation 2: talking to the doctor and billing
docs.text: DoctorYour father is stable now. The ECG shows a minor blockage. YouThank you, doctor. What does that mean? Is it serious? DoctorIt needs treatment, but we caught it early. We'd like to admit him for two days for tests. YouOkay. What tests will you do? DoctorBlood tests and an angiogram. Then we'll decide the next step. YouWhat's the estimated cost, and is it covered by insurance? DoctorThe billing desk will give you an estimate. Most of it should be covered. At the billing desk YouHi, I need an estimate for my father, Ramesh Gupta, admitted in ICU bed 4. StaffIt's about ₹85,000 for two days. We've sent the cashless request to your insurer. YouHow long does the insurance approval take? StaffUsually four to six hours. We'll inform you. YouThank you. Could you give me the estimate in writing?

docs.title: Visiting a patient
docs.text:
• "Which ward is Mr. Ramesh Gupta in? He was admitted yesterday."
  • "How is he doing today?"
  • "Can I bring him home-cooked food?"
  • "Is there anything he needs?"
  • (To the patient) "How are you feeling? Get well soon. Take rest."

docs.title: When things go wrong
docs.text:
• "We've been waiting for two hours. Could you tell us how long it will be?"
  • "The bill has charges for tests that weren't done."
  • "The insurance approval is taking too long. Who can I speak to?"
  • "I'd like a second opinion."

docs.text: Write the 5 facts a nurse needs in an emergency: name & age, problem, since when, conditions & medicines, allergies.

docs.title: At the Hotel
docs.text: Polite + specific = fast service. Front-desk staff solve problems all day. Make yours easy to solve.

docs.title: Check-in
docs.text:
They ask You say "Do you have a reservation?" "Yes, under the name Ashish Gupta, for 3 nights." "May I see your ID and a card for incidentals?" "Sure. Is the deposit refundable at check-out?" "Would you like breakfast included?" "How much extra is it per day?"

You can ask:

  • "What time is check-out? Is late check-out available?"
  • "What's the Wi-Fi password?"
  • "What time is breakfast, and where?"
  • "Could I have a quiet room / high floor / away from the lift?"
  • "Is there an airport shuttle? What time does it leave?"
  • "Do you have a gym / laundry service / business centre?"
  • "Can I leave my luggage here after check-out?"

docs.title: Problems with the room
docs.text:
"Hi, this is room 512. The AC isn't cooling, and the room is quite warm. Could you send someone to check it, or move me to another room? Thank you."

Other requests:

  • "The hot water isn't working."
  • "There's a lot of noise from the next room. Could you help?"

docs.title: Check-out

docs.title: Checking in early
docs.text: ReceptionistGood morning, welcome to the Residency. How can I help you? YouGood morning. I have a reservation under Ashish Gupta for three nights. ReceptionistYes, I have it. Check-in is at 2 pm, though. YouMy flight landed early. Is early check-in possible? ReceptionistLet me check… A room will be ready at 11. Would you like to leave your bags here? YouYes, please. Is breakfast still available? ReceptionistYes, until 10:30 in the restaurant on the first floor. YouGreat. And what's the Wi-Fi password? ReceptionistIt's on this card. Here's your key once the room is ready.

docs.title: A problem with the room
docs.text: YouHi, this is room 512. The AC isn't cooling, and the room is very warm. ReceptionistI'm sorry. I'll send a technician right away. Twenty minutes later YouHi again. The technician says the AC needs a part, and it can't be fixed today. ReceptionistI apologise. We can move you to another room on the 6th floor. YouThat would be great. Is it also non-smoking? ReceptionistYes, it is. Someone will help you with your bags. YouThank you. I appreciate the quick help.

docs.title: Day 33 · Insurance
docs.text: Day33Phase 3 · Everyday Life · Day 33 of 80 Done

docs.title: Insurance
docs.text:
Today's goal: ask the right questions before buying health, life, motor or travel insurance, make a claim clearly, and follow up when a claim is delayed or rejected.

Read the policy wording

Cover, exclusions and claim rules depend on the insurer and the plan. Before buying, ask for the policy wording and exclusions in writing, and check claims with the insurer's official helpline.

docs.title: Key words
docs.text: Word / phrase Meaning premium what you pay (monthly / yearly) sum insured / cover the maximum the insurer pays policyholder / insured / nominee who owns it / who's covered / who receives money term plan / health / motor / travel insurance policy types waiting period time before some illnesses are covered pre-existing disease (PED) illness you had before buying exclusions what is NOT covered co-pay / deductible your share of the bill cashless / reimbursement insurer pays the hospital / you pay and claim later network hospital / garage partner hospital or garage for cashless claims no-claim bonus (NCB) discount or extra cover for years without claims claim settlement / rejection / grievance outcome of a claim / complaint

docs.title: Questions to ask before buying
docs.text:
HealthLife (term)Motor & travel
  • What is the waiting period for pre-existing diseases?
  • Is there a room-rent limit or co-payment?
  • Which hospitals near me are in the cashless network?
  • Are maternity / OPD / day-care treatments covered?
  • What are the main exclusions?
  • Is the premium likely to increase with age?
  • How much cover do you recommend for my income and loans?
  • Until what age does the cover last?
  • What happens if I miss a premium payment?
  • What is the claim settlement ratio of the insurer?
  • Is zero depreciation included? Is roadside assistance included?
  • How does the no-claim bonus work if I make a small claim?
  • (Travel) Does it cover medical emergencies, flight delays and lost baggage?
  • (Travel) Is it accepted for my visa application?

docs.title: Conversation 1: buying health insurance
docs.text: AgentHello, this is Rohan from SafeLife Insurance. You requested a callback about health insurance. YouYes, thanks. I'm looking for a family floater for me, my wife and my son. AgentSure. What cover are you looking for? YouAbout ₹10 lakh. Before we talk about the price, could you tell me the waiting period for pre-existing diseases? AgentThree years for pre-existing diseases, and 30 days for new illnesses, except accidents. YouMy wife has thyroid. Will that be covered after three years? AgentYes, if you declare it now. YouIs there a room-rent limit or a co-payment? AgentNo room-rent limit, and no co-payment below age 60. YouWhich hospitals near Whitefield are cashless? AgentI'll email you the list. The premium is about ₹21,000 a year. YouCould you also email the policy wording and the list of exclusions? I'd like to read them before deciding. AgentSure, I'll send everything today.

docs.title: Conversation 2: following up on a delayed claim
docs.text: AgentThank you for calling. How can I help you? YouHi. I submitted a reimbursement claim three weeks ago, and there's no update. The claim number is CLM-448190. AgentLet me check… It's pending because the discharge summary is missing. YouI uploaded it on the 5th. Could you check again, please? AgentYou're right, I can see it now. It wasn't linked to the claim. I'll link it. YouThank you. How long will the settlement take now? AgentWithin seven working days. YouCould you send me an email confirming that the documents are complete? AgentYes, I'll send it now. YouAnd if it's rejected, what's the grievance process? AgentYou can write to our grievance team. The details are in the email. YouThank you, Priya. That's very helpful.

docs.title: When things go wrong
docs.text:
• "My claim was rejected as a pre-existing disease, but I declared it when I bought the policy. I'd like it reviewed."
  • "The hospital says the cashless approval hasn't come yet. Could you check?"
  • "My premium has gone up by 40%. Could you explain why?"
  • "I'd like to port my policy to another insurer. What's the process?"

docs.title: Practice
docs.text:
Write 5 questions you'd ask before buying a health insurance policy for your parents.

Sample answers

What's the waiting period for pre-existing diseases? · Is there a co-payment for senior citizens? · Is there a room-rent limit? · Which hospitals near their home are cashless? · How much will the premium increase each year?

docs.text:

docs.title: Metro & Bus
docs.text: Today's goal: buy tickets or cards, find the right route, ask where to get off, and handle crowded or confusing rides on the metro and city buses.

docs.title: Key words
docs.text: Word / phrase Meaning smart card / travel card a card you top up and tap at the gate top up / recharge add money to the card token / single-journey ticket one-time ticket line (Purple Line, Line 2) a metro route interchange / change at… station where you switch lines towards / direction which way the train is going ("towards Whitefield") platform / gate / exit where you board / enter / leave bus stop / bus stand / depot where buses stop / start route number the bus number (e.g. 500D) conductor person who sells tickets on the bus pass (daily / monthly) unlimited travel for a period rush hour / peak hours busiest times

docs.title: Questions you'll ask
docs.text:
MetroBus
  • How much is a ticket to MG Road?
  • Can I top up my card here?
  • Which line goes to the airport?
  • Do I need to change trains? Where do I change?
  • Which platform for trains towards Whitefield?
  • How many stops is it to Indiranagar?
  • Which exit is closest to the bus stand?
  • What time is the last train tonight?
  • Does this bus go to the railway station?
  • Which bus should I take for Koramangala?
  • How often does the 500D come?
  • How much is the fare to Silk Board?
  • Could you tell me when we get to the hospital stop?
  • Is this the right stop for the airport bus?
  • Where should I get off for the market?

docs.title: Questions you'll be asked
docs.text: They ask You answer Where to? MG Road, please. One ticket. Single or return? Single, please. Do you have a card? Yes, I'd like to top it up with ₹500. Do you have change? Sorry, I only have a ₹500 note. Can I pay by UPI? Ticket? (conductor) Here's my pass. / One to Majestic, please.

docs.title: Conversation 1: at the metro ticket counter
docs.text: YouHi. I'd like a ticket to Cubbon Park, please. ClerkSingle journey? YouYes. Actually, I'll be travelling every day. Can I get a smart card instead? ClerkSure. The card is ₹50, and you can add any amount. YouGreat. Please add ₹500. Can I pay by UPI? ClerkYes, scan here. YouDone. Which platform should I go to for Cubbon Park? ClerkPlatform 1, towards Challaghatta. It's four stops. YouDo I need to change trains? ClerkNo, it's direct. YouThank you!

docs.title: Conversation 2: on the bus, not sure where to get off
docs.text: YouExcuse me, does this bus go to St. John's Hospital? ConductorYes. Ticket? YouOne to St. John's, please. How much is it? Conductor₹25. YouHere you go. Could you tell me when we get there? I'm not from this area. ConductorOkay, it's about fifteen minutes. Twenty minutes later YouExcuse me, have we passed the hospital stop? PassengerNo, it's the next one, after the signal. YouThank you so much! ConductorHospital stop! Get down here. YouThanks!

docs.title: When things go wrong
docs.text:
• "The gate isn't opening. My card has balance. Could you check it?"
  • "I tapped in but forgot to tap out. What should I do?"
  • "I took the wrong direction. How do I go back to Majestic?"
  • "Sorry, is anyone sitting here?" / "Could you move in a little, please?"
  • "Excuse me, I need to get off at the next stop."

docs.title: Practice
docs.text:
Make questions for these answers:

  1. ______? → No, you need to change at Majestic.
  2. ______? → Every ten minutes.
  3. ______? → Take exit B, it's right next to the bus stand.
Answers
  1. Is this train direct to the airport? / Do I need to change trains?
  2. How often does the bus/train come? 3. Which exit is closest to the bus stand?

docs.title: Movies & Weekend Plans
docs.text: Today's goal: make plans with friends, book tickets, talk about films and shows, and give opinions and recommendations.

docs.title: Making plans
docs.text: Suggest Respond Do you want to watch a movie this weekend? Sure! Which one? How about Saturday evening? Saturday works for me. / Sunday is better for me. Shall we go for the 7 pm show? Perfect. Let's meet at the mall at 6:30. See you there! Are you up for a trek on Sunday? I'd love to, but I'm a bit tired. Maybe next week?

docs.title: Booking tickets
docs.text:
• "Two tickets for the 7:15 show, please. Recliner seats if available."
  • "Are there any seats in the middle row?"
  • "Is there a discount on weekdays?"
  • "Can I cancel the booking if plans change?"

docs.title: Talking about films and shows
docs.text:
Ask Answer What kind of movies do you like? I like thrillers and comedies. Not horror! What's it about? It's about a cricketer who makes a comeback after an injury. Who's in it? It stars… and it's directed by… How was it? It was brilliant / okay / a bit slow / too long. Would you recommend it? Definitely, especially the second half. / Not really, wait for it on OTT. Have you watched…? Yes, I loved it! / No, is it good?

Opinion words: gripping, hilarious, touching, predictable, slow, overrated, a must-watch, no spoilers, please!

docs.title: Conversation 1: making weekend plans
docs.text: FriendAny plans for the weekend? YouNot yet. Do you want to watch the new Malayalam thriller? Everyone's talking about it. FriendSure! Is it in theatres or on OTT? YouIn theatres. How about the 7 pm show on Saturday? FriendSaturday works. Should we have dinner after? YouGood idea. There's a nice Chettinad place near the mall. FriendPerfect. Will you book the tickets? YouYes, I'll book two recliners and send you the details.

docs.title: Conversation 2: after the movie
docs.text: FriendSo, what did you think? YouI loved it! The first half was a bit slow, but the twist at the interval was brilliant. FriendI know! I didn't see it coming at all. YouAnd the background music was amazing. Who was the composer? FriendSushin Shyam, I think. What did you think of the ending? YouHonestly, a little predictable. But overall, it's a must-watch. FriendAgreed. Should we watch the director's earlier film on Netflix next weekend? YouSure, let's do that!

docs.title: Neighbours & Society
docs.text: Today's goal: get to know your neighbours, ask for and offer help, handle complaints (noise, parking, leaks) politely, and speak up at a residents' association meeting.

docs.title: Key words
docs.text: Word / phrase Meaning neighbour / next door / upstairs / downstairs people near you residents' welfare association (RWA) / society building management group secretary / committee / AGM RWA roles / annual meeting common area / clubhouse / lift / parking shared spaces maintenance charges monthly fee for the building complaint / request / notice formal messages

docs.title: Friendly phrases
docs.text:
• "Hi, I'm Ashish from 304. We just moved in."
  • "If you ever need anything, just knock."
  • "Could I borrow a ladder for ten minutes?"
  • "Could you collect my parcel if it comes while I'm out?"
  • "We're having a small get-together on Saturday. Would you like to come?"

docs.title: Complaining politely: the 3 Fs
docs.text: Friendly opening → Fact (what happened) → Fix (a polite request) ❌ Rude ✅ Polite "Your music is too loud. Stop it." "Hi! Sorry to bother you. The music is quite loud in our flat, and my kids are trying to sleep. Could you turn it down a little after 10?" "Don't park in my spot." "Hi, I think your car is in my parking spot, number 12. Could you move it when you get a chance?"

docs.title: Conversation 1: noise from upstairs
docs.text: YouHi, I'm Ashish from 304, just below you. Sorry to disturb you. NeighbourOh, hi! No problem. Is everything okay? YouYes, mostly. It's just that we hear a lot of furniture moving late at night, around 11 or 12. NeighbourOh, I'm sorry! We've been rearranging the rooms. I didn't realise it was so loud. YouNo worries. My daughter has exams, so she sleeps early. Could you avoid it after 10? NeighbourOf course. We'll put felt pads under the chairs too. YouThat's really kind of you. Thank you! NeighbourThanks for telling us nicely.

docs.title: Conversation 2: speaking at the society meeting
docs.text: SecretaryAny other points from residents? YouYes, I'd like to raise one point about parking. SecretaryPlease go ahead. YouMany visitors are parking in residents' spots, especially on weekends. Last Sunday, three of us couldn't park. ResidentThat's true. It's happened to me too. YouI'd like to suggest two things: visitor parking stickers, and the security guard asking visitors to use the visitor area. SecretaryThat sounds reasonable. Do we have a cost estimate for the stickers? YouI checked. It's about ₹2,000 for 500 stickers. I'm happy to coordinate it. SecretaryGreat. Let's vote on it. All in favour?

docs.title: Practice
docs.text:
Write a polite WhatsApp message to your neighbour about their dog barking all day while they're at work.

Sample answer

Hi Neha, hope you're well! Just wanted to let you know that Bruno barks quite a lot during the day when you're out. I work from home and it's been hard during calls. Is there anything that might help, like a dog walker in the afternoon? Thanks so much!

docs.title: Day 18 · Phone Calls
docs.text: Day18Phase 2 · Communication · Day 18 of 80 Done

docs.title: Phone Calls
docs.text: Phone calls are harder than face-to-face talk because you can't see the other person. Prepare 3 bullet points, speak slowly, and confirm everything at the end.

docs.title: Before you call
docs.text:
• Write your goal: "Reschedule appointment to Friday."
  • Have details ready: booking ID, account number, dates
  • Have pen & paper for reference numbers
  • Find a quiet place

docs.title: Opening the call
docs.text: "Hi, this is Ashish Gupta. I'm calling about my booking, reference 4X7Q2. I'd like to change the date to Friday the 14th."

docs.title: Useful phrases
docs.text: Situation Say Didn't hear "Sorry, the line's not clear. Could you repeat that?" Spelling "Could you spell that for me?" / "That's G for Goa, U for Umbrella…" Numbers "Let me read that back: 9-8-4-5…" Put on hold "Sure, I'll hold." Wrong department "Could you transfer me to the billing team, please?" Getting nowhere "I understand. Could I speak to a supervisor, please?" Ending "Just to confirm: the appointment is Friday at 3 pm, ref 4X7Q2. Thank you!"

docs.title: Work calls
docs.text:
• Start: "Hi Rahul, is now a good time? It'll take 5 minutes."
  • Unexpected call: "Can I call you back in 10 minutes? I'm just finishing something."
  • End: "Great, I'll send a quick email summarising what we agreed."

docs.title: Leaving a voicemail
docs.text:
"Hi, this is Ashish Gupta from XYZ Technologies. I'm calling about the invoice for October.
Please call me back on 98450-12345. Again, that's 98450-12345. Thanks!"

Name → reason → number (said twice, slowly) → thanks.

docs.title: Rescheduling an appointment

docs.title: Day 47 · Police & Emergencies
docs.text: Day47Phase 3 · Everyday Life · Day 47 of 80 Done

docs.title: Police & Emergencies
docs.text:
Today's goal: stay clear and calm in an emergency: call for help, report a theft or accident, and answer police questions with exact facts.

Emergency numbers (India)

112 all emergencies · 100 police · 101 fire · 108 ambulance (most states) · 1930 cyber-fraud helpline. Abroad, check the local number before you travel (911 US, 112 EU, 999 UK).

docs.title: The emergency call formula
docs.text:
What happened → exact location + landmark → who's hurt / in danger → your name & number

"There's been a road accident. A bike and a car have collided on Outer Ring Road, near the Marathahalli bridge, opposite the petrol pump. One man is bleeding from the head and isn't moving. My name is Ashish, and my number is 98450 12345."

docs.title: Key words
docs.text: Word / phrase Meaning FIR / complaint / report the official police record theft / stolen / pickpocketed / snatched taking your things accident / collision / hit-and-run road incidents witness someone who saw it fraud / scam / OTP / unauthorised transaction online crime injured / unconscious / bleeding medical state

docs.title: Questions you'll be asked
docs.text: Police ask You answer What happened? My phone was snatched by two men on a bike. When and where? About 8:30 pm today, outside the Indiranagar metro station, exit B. Can you describe them? Two young men, black helmets, a red bike. I couldn't see the number plate. What was stolen? An iPhone 14, black cover. Here's the IMEI number from the box. Were there any witnesses? A shopkeeper saw it. He's still there.

docs.title: Questions you'll ask
docs.text:
• How do I file an FIR / complaint?
  • Can I file it online?
  • Could I have a copy of the complaint / FIR number?
  • What should I do next? (block SIM, inform bank)
  • Will you inform me if you find anything?

docs.title: Conversation 1: reporting a stolen phone
docs.text: OfficerYes, what's the problem? YouI'd like to report a theft. My phone was snatched about an hour ago. OfficerWhere did it happen? YouOutside Indiranagar metro station, exit B, at around 8:30. OfficerDid you see the person? YouTwo men on a red bike. Both wore black helmets. OfficerOkay. Which phone, and do you have the IMEI number? YouAn iPhone 14. Here's the IMEI from the bill. I've already blocked my SIM. OfficerGood. Fill in this form. We'll register the complaint. YouCould I have a copy with the complaint number? I need it for insurance. OfficerYes, you'll get a copy. YouThank you, sir.

docs.title: Conversation 2: online fraud
docs.text: YouHello, is this the cyber-fraud helpline? Money was taken from my account without my permission. AgentHow much, and when? You₹25,000, about twenty minutes ago. I got a call from someone pretending to be from my bank, and I shared an OTP. I realise now it was a scam. AgentHave you informed your bank? YouNot yet. I called you first. AgentCall your bank right away and block your card. I'm registering your complaint now. What's the transaction ID? YouIt's UPI ref 6102 9933 4471. AgentYour complaint number is CYB-77120. Please also file a report on the cybercrime portal. YouThank you. I'll call the bank now.

docs.title: Stay calm: phrases that help
docs.text:
• "Please send help quickly. The address is…"
  • "I'll stay on the line."
  • "Is there anything I should do until the ambulance arrives?"
  • "Sorry, could you repeat that? I'm a bit shaken."

docs.text:

On the visitDuring your stay

docs.title: Conversation 1: visiting a flat
docs.text: OwnerCome in. This is the 2BHK. It's semi-furnished. YouIt's nice and bright. How much is the rent? Owner₹32,000 a month, plus ₹3,000 maintenance. YouAnd the deposit? OwnerSix months' rent. YouThat's quite high. Most places nearby ask for three months. Would you accept three? OwnerHmm, I can do four. YouOkay, four works. Is there power backup and 24-hour water? OwnerYes, both. YouIs there a lock-in period? OwnerEleven-month agreement, with a two-month notice period. YouCan we add in the agreement that the deposit is returned within 15 days of moving out? OwnerSure, that's fair. YouGreat. I'd like to move in on the 1st.

docs.title: Conversation 2: calling the landlord about a problem
docs.text: YouHi Mr. Reddy, this is Ashish from flat 302. Sorry to call on a Sunday. OwnerNo problem. What happened? YouThere's water leaking from the bathroom ceiling. It started last night, and it's getting worse. OwnerOh no. Is it from the flat above? YouI think so. I've put a bucket under it, and I've told the people upstairs. OwnerOkay. I'll send a plumber tomorrow morning. Will someone be home? YouI'll work from home tomorrow, so yes. Could you also check who will pay for the repair? OwnerIf it's from the upstairs pipe, they'll pay. Don't worry. YouThank you. Please send me the plumber's number.

docs.title: Before you sign: checklist
docs.text:
• Rent, maintenance, deposit, brokerage, all in writing
  • Lock-in and notice period
  • Who pays for which repairs
  • Photos/video of the flat's condition on move-in day
  • Meter readings noted on day one

docs.title: Practice
docs.text:
Negotiate politely: the owner asks for 10 months' deposit. Write your reply.

Sample answer

That's much higher than other flats in this area, which ask for three to four months. Would you consider four months? I'm happy to sign an 11-month agreement.

docs.title: Restaurant & Café
docs.text: Ordering food is a good confidence workout: short, friendly and low-risk. Team dinners and client lunches use the same phrases.

docs.title: Arriving

  • "We have a reservation under Gupta, 8 pm."

docs.title: Ordering
docs.text: Situation Say Need time "Could we have a few more minutes, please?" Ask for a recommendation "What do you recommend? What's popular here?" Dietary needs "I'm vegetarian / vegan / allergic to peanuts. Does this dish contain any?" Customise "Could I have this less spicy / without onions / sauce on the side?" Ordering "I'll have the paneer tikka, and could I get a lime soda?" Portion "Is this enough for two, or should we order more?" Coffee "A medium cappuccino with oat milk, please. For here / to go."

docs.title: During the meal
docs.text:
• "Excuse me, could we get some more water, please?"
  • "Sorry, this isn't what I ordered. I asked for the grilled fish."
  • "The food is a bit cold. Could you warm it up, please?"
  • "Everything was delicious, thank you!"

docs.title: The bill
docs.text:
• "Could we have the bill / the check, please?"
  • "Can we split the bill?" / "I'll get this one."
  • "Do you accept cards / UPI?"
  • "Is service charge included?"

Hosting a client / team dinner

Let guests order first. Suggest 2–3 dishes if they're unsure. Avoid heavy work talk until the food arrives. Settle the bill quietly (tell the waiter in advance, or step away to pay).

docs.title: Ordering with dietary needs
docs.text: WaiterGood evening. Are you ready to order? YouAlmost. Could you tell me what's in the chef's special curry? WaiterIt has paneer, cashews and cream. YouMy friend is allergic to nuts. Can it be made without cashews? WaiterYes, we can do that. YouGreat. We'll have one chef's special without cashews, one dal tadka, and four rotis. WaiterAnything to drink? YouTwo sweet lassis, please. And could we have some water? WaiterSure. Anything else? YouThat's all for now, thank you.

docs.title: Wrong order and the bill
docs.text: YouExcuse me, I think this isn't what we ordered. We asked for dal tadka, not dal makhani. WaiterI'm so sorry. I'll change it right away. YouThank you. Later YouCould we have the bill, please? WaiterHere you are. YouI think we've been charged for the dal makhani as well. WaiterYou're right, I apologise. I'll correct it. YouNo problem. Can we pay by UPI? And is the service charge included? WaiterYes, UPI is fine, and the service charge is included. YouThank you. The food was delicious.

docs.title: Day 17 · Small Talk & Networking
docs.text: Day17Phase 2 · Communication · Day 17 of 80 Done

docs.title: Small Talk & Networking
docs.text: Small talk is how people start to trust each other. Most opportunities (jobs, partnerships, mentors) start with a 3-minute chat. Ask, listen, follow up.

docs.title: The 4-step conversation
docs.text: 1. Open — comment on the shared situation 2. Ask — open questions about them 3. Connect — find something in common, share a little 4. Exit — gracefully, with a next step

docs.title: Openers
docs.text:
Conference / meetupOffice / new teamTravel (airport, train, flight)Waiting / lift / café
  • "Hi, I'm Ashish. What did you think of that talk?"
  • "What brings you here today?"
  • "Is this your first time at this conference?"
  • "Hi, I don't think we've met. I'm Ashish, I work on the checkout team."
  • "How was your weekend?"
  • "Are you working on anything exciting this quarter?"
  • "Are you travelling for work or holiday?"
  • "Have you been to Singapore before? Any tips?"
  • "This delay is long, isn't it? Where are you heading?"

docs.title: Introduce yourself (networking pitch)
docs.text:
"I'm Ashish. I'm a backend engineer working on a grocery marketplace. Lots of Kafka and microservices. Lately I've been figuring out how to make checkout reliable during flash sales. What about you?"

Keep it short and interesting, and end with a question back to them.

docs.title: Day 21 · Travel Visa
docs.text: Day21Phase 3 · Everyday Life · Day 21 of 80 Done

docs.title: Travel Visa
docs.text:
Today's goal: understand visa types, ask the right questions about documents and timelines, and answer visa-interview questions clearly, briefly and honestly. You'll need all of this before you book the flight.

Rules differ by country

Visa types, documents, fees and processing times change often and depend on the country you're visiting and your passport. Always check the official embassy or consulate website, or the official visa application centre, before you apply. This page is about communication.

docs.title: Key words
docs.text: Word / phrase Meaning tourist / business / work / student / transit visa visa types single-entry / multiple-entry enter once / many times validity / duration of stay how long the visa is valid / how long you may stay each visit embassy / consulate / visa application centre (VAC) where visas are handled appointment / biometrics booked slot / fingerprints and photo invitation letter / sponsor a letter from the host / person or company paying itinerary / travel insurance / hotel booking travel plan documents bank statements / ITR / salary slips proof of funds and income no-objection certificate (NOC) / leave letter letter from your employer approved / refused / administrative processing visa results

docs.title: Questions you'll ask
docs.text:
Before applyingAt the visa centre
  • Which visa type do I need for a two-day client meeting?
  • What documents do I need? Is there a checklist?
  • How long does processing take? Can I apply for priority processing?
  • How early can I apply before my travel date?
  • Do I need an appointment for biometrics?
  • Do I need travel insurance? What's the minimum cover?
  • How much is the fee, and how do I pay?
  • Where do I submit my documents?
  • Do you need the originals or only copies?
  • Can I keep my passport while the visa is processed?
  • How will I know when the passport is ready to collect?
  • Can someone else collect my passport?

docs.title: Visa interview: questions you'll be asked
docs.text:
Golden rule: answer exactly what's asked, briefly and honestly, and have documents ready.

Officer asks Good answer What's the purpose of your trip? I'm attending a three-day product workshop at our client's office in Berlin. Who is paying for the trip? My company is paying. Here's the invitation and the letter from my employer. How long will you stay? Five days, from the 10th to the 15th of March. Where will you stay? At the Hotel Adlon, near the client's office. Here's the booking. What do you do? I'm a senior software engineer at XYZ Technologies in Bengaluru. I've been there for six years. Why should we believe you'll return? I have a permanent job, my family lives in Bengaluru, and I have a return ticket for the 15th. Have you travelled abroad before? Yes, to Singapore in 2023 and to Dubai in 2024, both for work. Do you have relatives there? No, I don't. / Yes, my cousin lives in Munich, but I'm staying at the hotel.

Don't

Memorise long speeches · give extra information that wasn't asked for · guess dates or numbers · say anything you can't prove. If you don't understand, say: "Sorry, could you repeat the question?"

docs.title: Conversation 1: at the visa application centre
docs.text: StaffGood morning. Appointment letter and passport, please. YouGood morning. Here you are. I'm applying for a business visa for Germany. StaffDo you have the document checklist? YouYes. Everything is in this folder, in the same order as the checklist. StaffThank you. The invitation letter is a copy. Do you have the original? YouThe client sent it by email. Is a printed copy acceptable? StaffFor this category, yes. Please sign here. Next, go to counter 4 for biometrics. YouOkay. How long does processing usually take? StaffAbout 15 working days. You'll get an SMS when the passport is ready. YouCan I track the status online? StaffYes, with the reference number on this receipt. YouThank you very much.

docs.title: Conversation 2: the visa interview
docs.text: OfficerGood morning. What's the purpose of your trip to the United States? YouGood morning. I'm attending a five-day technical conference in Seattle. OfficerWho is paying for the trip? YouMy company. Here's the letter from my employer. OfficerHow long have you worked there? YouSix years. I'm a senior engineer on the payments team. OfficerAre you married? YouYes. My wife and my son live with me in Bengaluru. OfficerHave you been to the US before? YouNo, this is my first time. I've travelled to Singapore and Dubai for work. OfficerWhen are you coming back? YouOn the 22nd of June. My return ticket is booked. OfficerOkay. Your visa is approved. You'll get your passport back by courier. YouThank you!

docs.title: Follow-up and problems
docs.text:
• "My application has been in processing for 25 days. Could you tell me if anything is missing?"
  • "My travel date is next week. Is it possible to expedite the application?"
  • "My visa was refused. Could you tell me the reason, and can I reapply?"
  • "There's a spelling mistake in my name on the visa. How do I get it corrected?"

docs.title: Practice
docs.text:
Answer these in one sentence each, for a trip you'd like to take: purpose, length of stay, who pays, your job, why you'll return.

Sample answers

I'm visiting Japan on holiday with my family. · Ten days, from the 3rd to the 13th of April. · I am, from my savings; here are my bank statements. · I'm a software engineer at XYZ Technologies. · I have a permanent job and my parents live with me here; my return ticket is booked.

docs.title: Day 16 · Building Confidence
docs.text: Day16Phase 2 · Communication · Day 16 of 80 Done

docs.title: Building Confidence
docs.text: Confidence doesn't come before action. It comes from repeating the action. You don't need to feel confident to act confident. The feeling follows the practice.

docs.title: Why you feel nervous (and why it's normal)
docs.text:
• Fear of judgement: "They'll think I don't know enough." Most people are thinking about themselves, not about you.
  • Language anxiety: speaking in a second language makes everyone feel slower. Clear, simple English beats fancy English every time.
  • Impostor syndrome: common among experienced developers too. A 15-year engineer may know the code well and still feel lost in a room of executives.
  • Lack of preparation: this is the most common cause, and the easiest one to fix.

docs.title: The confidence loop
docs.text: 1. Prepare — write 3 bullet points before any important conversation 2. Act — speak up once, even briefly 3. Survive — notice that nothing terrible happened 4. Reflect — one thing that went well, one to improve 5. Repeat — each loop makes the next one easier

docs.title: 10 practical habits
docs.text:
1. Speak in the first 5 minutes of every meeting. Even "Good morning, everyone" or "I agree with Rahul's point" counts. The longer you wait, the harder it gets.
  2. Prepare 3 bullet points before any 1:1, demo, or difficult conversation.
  3. Slow down by 20%. Nervous people speak fast. A slow pace sounds calm and senior.
  4. Pause instead of filling. Swap "umm" for a 1-second pause. Pauses sound thoughtful.
  5. Stop over-apologising. Keep "sorry" for real mistakes. Swap "Sorry for the delay" for "Thanks for your patience."
  6. Keep a wins file. Write down every bug you fixed, compliment you got, problem you solved. Read it before reviews and interviews.
  7. Say "I don't know — I'll find out by X." It's a confident sentence.
  8. Record yourself explaining a concept for 2 minutes. Watch it once. You'll fix 3 habits immediately.
  9. Volunteer for small visibility: a 5-minute demo, a stand-up summary, a lunch-and-learn.
  10. Talk to strangers in low-stakes places: a café, a train, an airport. It trains the same muscle you use at work. See Everyday Life.

docs.title: Body language and voice
docs.text:
Signal Low confidence High confidence Posture Hunched, arms crossed Upright, shoulders relaxed, open hands Eyes Looking down or at the screen Natural eye contact (3–5 s, then look away) Voice Rising tone at the end ("It's done?") Falling tone at the end ("It's done.") Pace Rushed, no pauses Steady, with pauses before key points Hands Fidgeting, touching face Still, or gesturing at waist level Video calls Camera off, mic muted until called Camera on, eyes on lens when making a point

The 2-minute reset (before a big meeting)

  1. Stand up. Roll your shoulders back.
  2. Breathe in for 4, hold for 4, out for 6, three times.
  3. Say your first sentence out loud once.
  4. Remind yourself: "I'm here because I know something useful."

docs.title: Reframes for negative self-talk
docs.text: Thought Reframe "My English isn't good enough." "Clear and simple is enough. People care about the idea." "They'll find out I don't know everything." "Nobody knows everything. Asking good questions is a senior skill." "I made a mistake in that meeting." "I noticed it, so I can fix it next time. That's growth." "I'm too junior to speak to the CEO." "The CEO wants information from people closest to the work. That's me." "I've been doing this 15 years, I should be better at this." "Communication is a separate skill. I can learn it just like I learned a new framework."

docs.title: Confidence for experienced engineers
docs.text:
Seniors have a different trap. They know so much that they over-explain, get defensive about legacy decisions, or go quiet among executives. Try:

  • Be brief on purpose. Your expertise shows in what you choose to leave out.
  • Say "I was wrong" in public. Admitting a mistake makes you look more credible, not less.
  • Sponsor, don't just mentor: speak juniors' names in rooms they're not in.
  • Ask for feedback on your communication, not just your code.

docs.title: Practice conversation: Speaking up early in a meeting
docs.text: LeadLet's start. Any updates before we discuss the roadmap? YouYes, one quick update. The search API is live in staging, and it's 40% faster. LeadGreat news. Any risks? YouOne. The old mobile app version doesn't support it, so we'll need a fallback for about two weeks. LeadGood point. Can you write that up? YouSure, I'll share it after this meeting.

docs.title: Day 78 · Burnout & Wellbeing
docs.text: Day78Phase 5 · Career · Day 78 of 80 Done

docs.title: Burnout & Wellbeing
docs.text:
Burnout is not a sign of weakness, and it isn't solved by working harder. It builds slowly, until work that used to energise you starts to drain you. This page covers how to spot it, how to talk about it, and how to recover, whether it's you or someone on your team.

This is a communication guide, not medical advice

If you feel persistently hopeless, can't sleep or function, or have thoughts of harming yourself, please talk to a doctor or mental-health professional, or reach a crisis helpline in your country right away. Many companies also offer a free, confidential Employee Assistance Programme (EAP): ask HR. Reaching out early is the right move.

docs.title: What burnout looks like
docs.text:
Burnout is commonly described as having three parts:

Exhaustion — tired all the time; rest doesn't refill the tank Cynicism — "Why bother?"; distance from work, team and users Reduced effectiveness — simple tasks feel hard; you doubt your skills

docs.title: Warning signs to watch for
docs.text: In yourself In a teammate Dreading Monday from Saturday Camera off, quieter in meetings Working longer but getting less done Messages at midnight and weekends Irritable over small things Short, sharp replies; more conflict Can't switch off; checking Slack in bed Missing deadlines they used to hit easily No energy for hobbies, family, exercise Cancelling leave; "I'll rest after this release" Headaches, poor sleep, getting sick often Cynical jokes about the work or company

docs.title: Common causes in tech
docs.text:
• Workload: permanent crunch, too many priorities, never-ending on-call
  • Lack of control: shifting requirements, decisions made without you
  • Lack of recognition: effort goes unnoticed
  • Unfairness: some people carry the team, others don't
  • Values conflict: being asked to ship things you believe are wrong
  • Isolation: remote work without real connection

docs.title: Talking to your manager
docs.text:
The hardest step is often saying it out loud. You don't have to use the word "burnout" if it doesn't feel right. Describe the impact and ask for specific changes.

Raising itAsking for specific changesIf you need time offIf the response is dismissive

"I want to be honest with you about something. For the last couple of months I've been running on empty. I'm working late most nights, and I'm still falling behind, and it's starting to affect my sleep and the quality of my work. I'd like to figure out together how to make this sustainable."

"A few things would really help: taking me off the on-call rota for the next month, and dropping or delaying the reporting feature so I can focus on the migration. And I'd like to take a week off after the release on the 15th."

Come with 2–3 concrete requests. It's much easier for a manager to say yes to something specific.

"I need to take some time off to recover. I've spoken to my doctor, and I'll be on medical leave for two weeks starting Monday. I'll hand over my current work to Ravi tomorrow."

You don't owe anyone medical details. "Health reasons" is enough.

"I understand there's a lot of pressure on the team. But if nothing changes, I won't be able to keep doing my best work, and I want to. Can we look at the priorities together this week?"

If it continues, talk to HR, your skip-level manager, or the EAP. Your health comes first.

docs.title: Recovering: what actually helps
docs.text:
• Real rest: leave without laptop or Slack, not "working holidays"
  • Sleep first: consistent sleep and wake times; no screens in the last hour
  • Move your body: a daily walk counts
  • Hard stop each day: a fixed logoff time and a shutdown ritual
  • Reduce, don't just reorganise: drop work, don't only reprioritise it
  • Reconnect: friends, family and hobbies that have nothing to do with screens
  • Small wins: finish small, visible tasks to rebuild a sense of progress
  • Professional support: a therapist or counsellor; many EAPs offer free sessions

See Leave & Boundaries and Work from Home for scripts to protect your time.

docs.title: Prevention: daily and weekly habits
docs.text: Habit Why Say no (or "not now") to new work when full Workload is the biggest driver Take all your annual leave, spread across the year Recovery has to be regular Keep one non-work commitment every week It gives you a reason to stop Keep a wins file Counters the "nothing I do matters" feeling Have a weekly 1:1 with honest check-ins Problems get caught early Rotate on-call fairly; keep it compensated Prevents silent overload

docs.title: For team leads: spotting & supporting
docs.text:
Checking inTaking actionFixing the system

"I've noticed you've been online late a lot recently, and you seem a bit stretched. How are you doing, honestly? No judgement. I'd rather know early so I can help."

Then listen. Don't jump straight to fixes. Ask: "What would help most right now?"

  • Remove work, not just "take care of yourself": reassign tasks, push deadlines, pause on-call
  • Insist on leave for people who keep postponing it, and don't contact them during it
  • Protect them from escalations for a while
  • Follow up weekly, quietly
  • Track overtime, after-hours messages and on-call load as team health signals
  • Plan sprints at real capacity, around 70–80% of theoretical
  • Push back on leadership about unrealistic timelines (see Talking to the CEO)
  • Model it yourself: take leave, log off on time, don't send midnight messages

Don't say

  • "Everyone's tired, just push through this release."
  • "You should manage your time better."
  • "Let's talk about it after the launch."
  • "Just do some yoga." (on its own, without changing workload)

docs.title: A note for experienced engineers
docs.text: High performers are often the most at risk: you're trusted with everything, you find it hard to say no, and part of your identity is being the person who saves the day. Being sustainable is a senior skill. A team that depends on one person working late isn't a strong team, and fixing that is part of your job.

docs.title: Practice conversation: Telling your manager you're overloaded
docs.text: YouCan I be honest about something? I've been working late every night for a month, and I'm exhausted. ManagerThank you for telling me. I hadn't realised it was that bad. YouI'm worried it's affecting my work. I made two mistakes last week that I normally wouldn't. ManagerWhat would help most right now? YouMoving the reporting feature to next sprint, and taking me off on-call for two weeks. ManagerI can do both. And please take a few days off after the release. YouThank you. That really helps.

docs.title: Day 14 · Communication Principles
docs.text: Day14Phase 2 · Communication · Day 14 of 80 Done

docs.title: Communication Principles
docs.text: Communication is not what you say. It's what the other person understands. Seven rules, then frameworks you can reuse anywhere.

docs.title: The communication stack
docs.text:
Each layer depends on the one under it. Hover a layer to bring it forward.

6. Trust — built when layers 1–5 stay consistent over time 5. Confidence — steady voice, no over-apology, ownership 4. Tone — polite, firm, warm, matched to the moment 3. Structure — point first, then reasons, then the ask 2. Clarity — simple words, one idea per sentence 1. Listening — understand before you try to be understood

docs.title: 1. Lead with the point (BLUF: Bottom Line Up Front)
docs.text:
Developers often tell the story in order: "So I was looking at the logs, and then I noticed...". Busy listeners stop paying attention before the point arrives.

❌ Story first ✅ Point first "So yesterday I was debugging and I found the cache wasn't… and then I checked the config and…" "The release is blocked by a cache bug. I need 1 more day. Here's what happened…"

docs.title: 2. Know your audience: the altitude rule
docs.text:
Pitch the same issue at a different height for each listener:

Audience Cares about Talk about CEO / Exec Revenue, customers, risk, reputation Impact, decision needed, timeline Manager Delivery, team health, surprises Status, risks, options, what you need Peer engineer How it works, trade-offs Design, code, data Junior Learning, doing it right, not looking silly Steps, reasons, encouragement Customer / stranger Their problem solved Plain language, next step

docs.title: 3. One idea per sentence
docs.text: Short sentences sound confident. Long sentences sound like you're still working out what you think.

docs.title: 4. Specific beats vague
docs.text:
• Vague: "It's kind of slow." → Specific: "p95 latency went from 200 ms to 1.4 s after Tuesday's deploy."
  • Vague: "Soon." → Specific: "By Thursday 5 pm."

docs.title: 5. Always end with an ask or a next step
docs.text:
Every message should answer "what do you want from me?"

"…so can you approve the extra day?" · "…I'll update you at 4 pm." · "…no action needed, FYI only."

docs.title: 6. Polite ≠ weak. Firm ≠ rude.
docs.text: Too weak Balanced Too harsh "Sorry, I might be wrong, but maybe…" "I see it differently. Here's why." "That's wrong." "If it's okay, could I possibly…" "Could I take 10 minutes on this?" "I need this now."

docs.title: 7. Confirm understanding
docs.text: Close important conversations with a recap: "Just to confirm: I'll fix the cache by Thursday, and you'll tell the product team. Right?"

docs.title: Reusable frameworks
docs.text:
PREP (give an opinion)SBAR (report an issue)STAR (tell a story / interview)What / So what / Now what (status)

Point → Reason → Example → Point again

"I recommend Postgres over Mongo (P). Our data is relational: orders, items, payments (R). Last year's reporting rewrite took 3 months because of joins in Mongo (E). So Postgres is the safer choice (P)."

Situation → Background → Assessment → Recommendation

"Checkout is failing for 8% of users (S). It started after the 2 pm payment-SDK upgrade (B). I think the new SDK times out under load (A). I recommend we roll back now and investigate tomorrow (R)."

Situation → Task → Action → Result

"Our deploys took 2 hours (S). I was asked to cut that down (T). I parallelised the test suite and added caching (A). Deploys now take 18 minutes (R)."

What: API migration is 70% done. So what: We're on track, but the auth piece is risky. Now what: I'll pair with Priya on auth tomorrow; update on Friday.

docs.title: Words to cut and words to use
docs.text: Cut (filler / weak) Use instead basically, actually, like, you know (silence, a short pause) "I think maybe we could…" "I suggest we…" / "My recommendation is…" "Sorry to bother you" "Do you have 5 minutes for…?" "Does that make sense?" "What questions do you have?" "I'll try" "I will" / "I can't commit to that, but I can…" "It's not my fault" "Here's what happened and what I'm doing about it." "No problem" (after thanks) "Happy to help."

docs.title: Practice conversation: Point first, with your manager
docs.text: ManagerHow's the payment integration going? YouIt'll be one day late: Thursday instead of Wednesday. The bank's sandbox was down for six hours yesterday. ManagerOkay. Is anything else at risk? YouNo. The rest is on track, and the tests are done. ManagerDo you need anything from me? YouYes, could you ask the bank for a backup sandbox? Then it won't happen again. ManagerSure, I'll email them today.

docs.title: Day 79 · Your 90-Day Improvement Plan
docs.text: Day79Phase 5 · Career · Day 79 of 80 Done

docs.title: Improving Soft Skills: The 90-Day Plan
docs.text: What gets measured gets improved. Score yourself, pick your track, and spend 10–20 minutes a day on it.

docs.title: Step 1: Self-assessment
docs.text:
Score each from 1 (rarely) to 5 (always). Redo it every 30 days.

# Skill Score 1 I state my main point in the first sentence ☐ 2 I speak up in meetings without being asked ☐ 3 I can explain a technical issue to a non-technical person ☐ 4 I raise risks early, before they become problems ☐ 5 I say no or push back politely when needed ☐ 6 I give feedback that's specific and kind ☐ 7 I listen without interrupting ☐ 8 I stay calm when someone is upset or criticises me ☐ 9 I can make small talk with a stranger for 3+ minutes ☐ 10 I write clear, short messages and emails ☐

10–25: Beginner track · 26–40: Intermediate track · 41–50: Advanced track

docs.title: Step 2: Choose your track
docs.text:
Beginner track Intermediate track Advanced track (8–15+ yrs)

Month 1: Foundations

  • Read Communication Principles and Building Confidence
  • Speak at least once in every meeting
  • Use the stand-up format every day
  • One 10-minute Master Prompt role-play a day
  • Learn 5 phrases a week from the Phrase Bank

Month 2: Workplace

  • Prepare an agenda for every 1:1 with your manager
  • Write one bug report using SBAR
  • Ask one clarifying question on every new task
  • Have a 5-minute conversation with someone outside your team each week

Month 3: Visibility

  • Give a 5-minute demo or knowledge-share
  • Practise one Everyday Life scenario in real life each week
  • Ask your manager: "What's one thing about how I communicate that I could improve?"

Month 1: Influence

  • Use PREP in every design discussion
  • Push back on one unrealistic estimate using options, not "no"
  • Mentor one junior with a weekly 30-minute session

Month 2: Up-level your audience

  • Write a one-page decision doc for a non-technical stakeholder
  • Present at a team-wide or cross-team meeting
  • Practise the CEO 30-second update with AI 5 times

Month 3: Hard conversations

  • Have one difficult conversation you've been avoiding
  • Run a blameless post-mortem
  • Get 360° feedback from a peer, a junior and your manager

Month 1: Executive presence

  • Shorten every update by 30%; lead with the decision
  • Pre-wire important meetings (talk to key people 1:1 beforehand)
  • Turn one technical proposal into a business case (cost, risk, revenue)

Month 2: Multiply others

  • Coach two people on communication, using this playbook
  • Delegate one high-visibility task and sponsor the person publicly
  • Facilitate (don't dominate) a design review: speak last

Month 3: External voice

  • Give a talk at a meetup or internal tech conference
  • Write a blog post or internal article
  • Practise the networking scripts at one event

docs.title: Step 3: Daily 10-minute drills
docs.text: Drill How Builds The 60-second explain Pick a concept (Kafka, caching, OAuth). Explain it aloud in 60 s to an imaginary 12-year-old. Clarity Rewrite one message Take a Slack message you sent. Make it 30% shorter with the point first. Brevity Shadowing Play a 1-minute clip of a good speaker (TED, a podcast). Repeat each sentence right after them. Fluency, pace Record & review Record a mock stand-up on your phone. Watch it once at 1x. Voice, fillers AI role-play Run the Master Prompt on today's real situation. Everything Word of the day Learn one professional phrase and use it in a real conversation. Vocabulary Reflection journal 3 lines: What I said · How it landed · What I'll try next. Self-awareness

docs.title: Step 4: Measure progress
docs.text:
• Redo the self-assessment every 30 days.
  • Count: how many times did you speak up this week? How many messages did you rewrite before sending?
  • Ask for feedback each quarter: "On a scale of 1–10, how clear are my updates? What would make them a 10?"

docs.title: Practice conversation: Asking for feedback on your communication
docs.text: YouCould I ask for some feedback? I'm working on my communication this quarter. ManagerOf course. YouOn a scale of 1 to 10, how clear are my updates in stand-ups? ManagerMaybe a 6. They're accurate, but sometimes too detailed. YouThat's helpful. What would make them a 9? ManagerStart with the result, then only the important detail. Keep it under a minute. YouOkay. I'll try that for the next two weeks. Could we check again at the end of the month? ManagerSure, let's do that.

docs.title: Day 15 · Listening & Asking Questions
docs.text: Day15Phase 2 · Communication · Day 15 of 80 Done

docs.title: Listening & Asking Questions
docs.text: Good listeners ask good questions, and people trust them more. Listening is the most underrated skill on this site.

docs.title: Active listening in 4 moves
docs.text:
1. Pay attention — close the laptop, look at them, don't plan your reply 2. Acknowledge — "Okay", "I see", a nod; show you're with them 3. Paraphrase — "So what you're saying is…" 4. Clarify — "When you say 'urgent', do you mean today or this week?"

Paraphrase in practice

Manager: "The client is unhappy, the dashboard keeps breaking and nobody tells them anything."

You: "So there are two problems: the dashboard's reliability, and how we communicate when it breaks. Which one hurts them more right now?"

docs.title: Question types and when to use them
docs.text: Type Example Use when Open "How do you see this working?" Exploring, building rapport Closed "Is the deadline Friday?" Confirming a fact Clarifying "What does 'done' mean for this ticket?" Requirements are vague Probing "What makes you say that?" Getting to the real reason Hypothetical "What if we shipped without the export feature?" Negotiating scope Reflective "It sounds like you're frustrated with the delays?" Emotions are high Summary "So we agreed X, Y, Z — right?" Closing a conversation

docs.title: Questions every developer should ask
docs.text:
Before starting a taskWhen you're stuckIn a 1:1With a stakeholder
  • What problem are we solving, and for whom?
  • What does done look like? How will we test it?
  • What is the deadline, and is it fixed or flexible?
  • Who else is affected? Who should review it?
  • Is there anything you've already tried or decided?
  • "I've tried A and B. Before I go further, am I on the right track?"
  • "Who knows the most about this module?"
  • "Can you point me to an example of how we usually do this?"
  • "What's the most important thing I should focus on this quarter?"
  • "What's one thing I could do better?"
  • "What does the next level look like for me?"
  • "What would success look like for you?"
  • "If we can only deliver one of these, which matters most?"
  • "What happens if this is a week late?"

docs.title: How to ask a "stupid" question without feeling stupid
docs.text:
Use the context + attempt + question pattern:

"I'm new to the payments module (context). I read the README and traced the refund() call (attempt), but I can't see where the ledger entry is created. Can you point me in the right direction? (question)"

It shows you put in effort first, and people respect that.

docs.title: Listening blockers to avoid
docs.text:
• Interrupting to show you already know the answer
  • Solving before the person has finished describing the problem
  • Checking your phone or Slack mid-conversation
  • "That's nothing, once I had…" (turning their story into yours)
  • Filling every silence; give people 3 seconds to think

docs.title: Practice conversation: Clarifying a vague request
docs.text: PMWe need the report page to be faster. Users are complaining. YouGot it. When you say faster, which part feels slow: opening the page, or downloading the report? PMMostly opening the page. It takes ages. YouRoughly how long? Five seconds, ten? PMAround twelve seconds for big customers. YouSo the goal is under three seconds for opening the page, for our biggest customers. Is that right? PMExactly. YouAnd is this needed for this release, or next month? PMNext month is fine.
